Project: Build a buffer pool manager in Python that mediates all access to a fixed-size on- disk page file (pages are fixed-width byte arrays addressed by page id) through a bounded set of in-memory frames. The pool has a configurable capacity of N frames and a page table mapping resident page_id -> frame. Expose: `fetch_page(page_id)` which returns a pinned frame (reading from disk on miss, evicting if the pool is full), `new_page()` which allocates a fresh page id and a pinned zeroed frame, `unpin_page(page_id, is_dirty)` which decrements the pin count and ORs in the dirty flag, `flush_page(page_id)` and `flush_all()` which write dirty frames back to disk and clear the dirty flag, and `delete_page(page_id)`. Eviction MUST use the LRU-K replacement policy (default K=2): track the last K access timestamps per frame, never evict a frame whose pin count is > 0, choose the victim with the largest backward k-distance (frames with fewer than K recorded accesses are treated as having infinite k-distance and are evicted first, tie-broken by least- recent access), and write the victim back to disk before reuse if it is dirty. A `fetch_page` that cannot find an unpinned, evictable frame must fail explicitly rather than overflow the pool. Persist nothing beyond the page file itself; correctness is about the cache discipline. Acceptance: the resident page count never exceeds N; a page is never evicted while pinned; a dirty page is always written to disk before its frame is reused and reading it back returns the last unpinned contents (no lost update); when frames have full access history the chosen victim matches a reference LRU-K computation, and an access pattern that defeats plain LRU (e.g. a single large scan amid a hot working set) must NOT evict the hot set under LRU-K; and a fetch with all frames pinned returns a clean failure. A scripted workload mixing scans, hot-key reuse, dirtying, and pin/unpin must agree with an independent oracle on every byte read back and on the exact eviction order.

  page_file.py: Low‑level fixed‑size page I/O on a single on‑disk file.

Project: Build a buffer pool manager in Python that mediates all access to a fixed-size on- disk page file (pages are fixed-width byte arrays addressed by page id) through a bounded set of in-memory frames. The pool has a configurable capacity of N frames and a page table mapping resident page_id -> frame. Expose: `fetch_page(page_id)` which returns a pinned frame (reading from disk on miss, evicting if the pool is full), `new_page()` which allocates a fresh page id and a pinned zeroed frame, `unpin_page(page_id, is_dirty)` which decrements the pin count and ORs in the dirty flag, `flush_page(page_id)` and `flush_all()` which write dirty frames back to disk and clear the dirty flag, and `delete_page(page_id)`. Eviction MUST use the LRU-K replacement policy (default K=2): track the last K access timestamps per frame, never evict a frame whose pin count is > 0, choose the victim with the largest backward k-distance (frames with fewer than K recorded accesses are treated as having infinite k-distance and are evicted first, tie-broken by least- recent access), and write the victim back to disk before reuse if it is dirty. A `fetch_page` that cannot find an unpinned, evictable frame must fail explicitly rather than overflow the pool. Persist nothing beyond the page file itself; correctness is about the cache discipline. Acceptance: the resident page count never exceeds N; a page is never evicted while pinned; a dirty page is always written to disk before its frame is reused and reading it back returns the last unpinned contents (no lost update); when frames have full access history the chosen victim matches a reference LRU-K computation, and an access pattern that defeats plain LRU (e.g. a single large scan amid a hot working set) must NOT evict the hot set under LRU-K; and a fetch with all frames pinned returns a clean failure. A scripted workload mixing scans, hot-key reuse, dirtying, and pin/unpin must agree with an independent oracle on every byte read back and on the exact eviction order.

Project: Build a buffer pool manager in Python that mediates all access to a fixed-size on- disk page file (pages are fixed-width byte arrays addressed by page id) through a bounded set of in-memory frames. The pool has a configurable capacity of N frames and a page table mapping resident page_id -> frame. Expose: `fetch_page(page_id)` which returns a pinned frame (reading from disk on miss, evicting if the pool is full), `new_page()` which allocates a fresh page id and a pinned zeroed frame, `unpin_page(page_id, is_dirty)` which decrements the pin count and ORs in the dirty flag, `flush_page(page_id)` and `flush_all()` which write dirty frames back to disk and clear the dirty flag, and `delete_page(page_id)`. Eviction MUST use the LRU-K replacement policy (default K=2): track the last K access timestamps per frame, never evict a frame whose pin count is > 0, choose the victim with the largest backward k-distance (frames with fewer than K recorded accesses are treated as having infinite k-distance and are evicted first, tie-broken by least- recent access), and write the victim back to disk before reuse if it is dirty. A `fetch_page` that cannot find an unpinned, evictable frame must fail explicitly rather than overflow the pool. Persist nothing beyond the page file itself; correctness is about the cache discipline. Acceptance: the resident page count never exceeds N; a page is never evicted while pinned; a dirty page is always written to disk before its frame is reused and reading it back returns the last unpinned contents (no lost update); when frames have full access history the chosen victim matches a reference LRU-K computation, and an access pattern that defeats plain LRU (e.g. a single large scan amid a hot working set) must NOT evict the hot set under LRU-K; and a fetch with all frames pinned returns a clean failure. A scripted workload mixing scans, hot-key reuse, dirtying, and pin/unpin must agree with an independent oracle on every byte read back and on the exact eviction order.

Project: Build a buffer pool manager in Python that mediates all access to a fixed-size on- disk page file (pages are fixed-width byte arrays addressed by page id) through a bounded set of in-memory frames. The pool has a configurable capacity of N frames and a page table mapping resident page_id -> frame. Expose: `fetch_page(page_id)` which returns a pinned frame (reading from disk on miss, evicting if the pool is full), `new_page()` which allocates a fresh page id and a pinned zeroed frame, `unpin_page(page_id, is_dirty)` which decrements the pin count and ORs in the dirty flag, `flush_page(page_id)` and `flush_all()` which write dirty frames back to disk and clear the dirty flag, and `delete_page(page_id)`. Eviction MUST use the LRU-K replacement policy (default K=2): track the last K access timestamps per frame, never evict a frame whose pin count is > 0, choose the victim with the largest backward k-distance (frames with fewer than K recorded accesses are treated as having infinite k-distance and are evicted first, tie-broken by least- recent access), and write the victim back to disk before reuse if it is dirty. A `fetch_page` that cannot find an unpinned, evictable frame must fail explicitly rather than overflow the pool. Persist nothing beyond the page file itself; correctness is about the cache discipline. Acceptance: the resident page count never exceeds N; a page is never evicted while pinned; a dirty page is always written to disk before its frame is reused and reading it back returns the last unpinned contents (no lost update); when frames have full access history the chosen victim matches a reference LRU-K computation, and an access pattern that defeats plain LRU (e.g. a single large scan amid a hot working set) must NOT evict the hot set under LRU-K; and a fetch with all frames pinned returns a clean failure. A scripted workload mixing scans, hot-key reuse, dirtying, and pin/unpin must agree with an independent oracle on every byte read back and on the exact eviction order.

Project: Build a buffer pool manager in Python that mediates all access to a fixed-size on- disk page file (pages are fixed-width byte arrays addressed by page id) through a bounded set of in-memory frames. The pool has a configurable capacity of N frames and a page table mapping resident page_id -> frame. Expose: `fetch_page(page_id)` which returns a pinned frame (reading from disk on miss, evicting if the pool is full), `new_page()` which allocates a fresh page id and a pinned zeroed frame, `unpin_page(page_id, is_dirty)` which decrements the pin count and ORs in the dirty flag, `flush_page(page_id)` and `flush_all()` which write dirty frames back to disk and clear the dirty flag, and `delete_page(page_id)`. Eviction MUST use the LRU-K replacement policy (default K=2): track the last K access timestamps per frame, never evict a frame whose pin count is > 0, choose the victim with the largest backward k-distance (frames with fewer than K recorded accesses are treated as having infinite k-distance and are evicted first, tie-broken by least- recent access), and write the victim back to disk before reuse if it is dirty. A `fetch_page` that cannot find an unpinned, evictable frame must fail explicitly rather than overflow the pool. Persist nothing beyond the page file itself; correctness is about the cache discipline. Acceptance: the resident page count never exceeds N; a page is never evicted while pinned; a dirty page is always written to disk before its frame is reused and reading it back returns the last unpinned contents (no lost update); when frames have full access history the chosen victim matches a reference LRU-K computation, and an access pattern that defeats plain LRU (e.g. a single large scan amid a hot working set) must NOT evict the hot set under LRU-K; and a fetch with all frames pinned returns a clean failure. A scripted workload mixing scans, hot-key reuse, dirtying, and pin/unpin must agree with an independent oracle on every byte read back and on the exact eviction order.

Project: Build a buffer pool manager in Python that mediates all access to a fixed-size on- disk page file (pages are fixed-width byte arrays addressed by page id) through a bounded set of in-memory frames. The pool has a configurable capacity of N frames and a page table mapping resident page_id -> frame. Expose: `fetch_page(page_id)` which returns a pinned frame (reading from disk on miss, evicting if the pool is full), `new_page()` which allocates a fresh page id and a pinned zeroed frame, `unpin_page(page_id, is_dirty)` which decrements the pin count and ORs in the dirty flag, `flush_page(page_id)` and `flush_all()` which write dirty frames back to disk and clear the dirty flag, and `delete_page(page_id)`. Eviction MUST use the LRU-K replacement policy (default K=2): track the last K access timestamps per frame, never evict a frame whose pin count is > 0, choose the victim with the largest backward k-distance (frames with fewer than K recorded accesses are treated as having infinite k-distance and are evicted first, tie-broken by least- recent access), and write the victim back to disk before reuse if it is dirty. A `fetch_page` that cannot find an unpinned, evictable frame must fail explicitly rather than overflow the pool. Persist nothing beyond the page file itself; correctness is about the cache discipline. Acceptance: the resident page count never exceeds N; a page is never evicted while pinned; a dirty page is always written to disk before its frame is reused and reading it back returns the last unpinned contents (no lost update); when frames have full access history the chosen victim matches a reference LRU-K computation, and an access pattern that defeats plain LRU (e.g. a single large scan amid a hot working set) must NOT evict the hot set under LRU-K; and a fetch with all frames pinned returns a clean failure. A scripted workload mixing scans, hot-key reuse, dirtying, and pin/unpin must agree with an independent oracle on every byte read back and on the exact eviction order.

Project: Build a buffer pool manager in Python that mediates all access to a fixed-size on- disk page file (pages are fixed-width byte arrays addressed by page id) through a bounded set of in-memory frames. Project: Build a buffer pool manager in Python that mediates all access to a fixed-size on- disk page file (pages are fixed-width byte arrays addressed by page id) through a bounded set of in-memory frames. The pool has a configurable capacity of N frames and a page table mapping resident page_id -> frame. Expose: `fetch_page(page_id)` which returns a pinned frame (reading from disk on miss, evicting if the pool is full), `new_page()` which allocates a fresh page id and a pinned zeroed frame, `unpin_page(page_id, is_dirty)` which decrements the pin count and ORs in the dirty flag, `flush_page(page_id)` and `flush_all()` which write dirty frames back to disk and clear the dirty flag, and `delete_page(page_id)`. Eviction MUST use the LRU-K replacement policy (default K=2): track the last K access timestamps per frame, never evict a frame whose pin count is > 0, choose the victim with the largest backward k-distance (frames with fewer than K recorded accesses are treated as having infinite k-distance and are evicted first, tie-broken by least- recent access), and write the victim back to disk before reuse if it is dirty. A `fetch_page` that cannot find an unpinned, evictable frame must fail explicitly rather than overflow the pool. Persist nothing beyond the page file itself; correctness is about the cache discipline. Acceptance: the resident page count never exceeds N; a page is never evicted while pinned; a dirty page is always written to disk before its frame is reused and reading it back returns the last unpinned contents (no lost update); when frames have full access history the chosen victim matches a reference LRU-K computation, and an access pattern that defeats plain LRU (e.g. a single large scan amid a hot working set) must NOT evict the hot set under LRU-K; and a fetch with all frames pinned returns a clean failure. A scripted workload mixing scans, hot-key reuse, dirtying, and pin/unpin must agree with an independent oracle on every byte read back and on the exact eviction order.

Project: Build a buffer pool manager in Python that mediates all access to a fixed-size on- disk page file (pages are fixed-width byte arrays addressed by page id) through a bounded set of in-memory frames. The pool has a configurable capacity of N frames and a page table mapping resident page_id -> frame. Expose: `fetch_page(page_id)` which returns a pinned frame (reading from disk on miss, evicting if the pool is full), `new_page()` which allocates a fresh page id and a pinned zeroed frame, `unpin_page(page_id, is_dirty)` which decrements the pin count and ORs in the dirty flag, `flush_page(page_id)` and `flush_all()` which write dirty frames back to disk and clear the dirty flag, and `delete_page(page_id)`. Eviction MUST use the LRU-K replacement policy (default K=2): track the last K access timestamps per frame, never evict a frame whose pin count is > 0, choose the victim with the largest backward k-distance (frames with fewer than K recorded accesses are treated as having infinite k-distance and are evicted first, tie-broken by least- recent access), and write the victim back to disk before reuse if it is dirty. A `fetch_page` that cannot find an unpinned, evictable frame must fail explicitly rather than overflow the pool. Persist nothing beyond the page file itself; correctness is about the cache discipline. Acceptance: the resident page count never exceeds N; a page is never evicted while pinned; a dirty page is always written to disk before its frame is reused and reading it back returns the last unpinned contents (no lost update); when frames have full access history the chosen victim matches a reference LRU-K computation, and an access pattern that defeats plain LRU (e.g. a single large scan amid a hot working set) must NOT evict the hot set under LRU-K; and a fetch with all frames pinned returns a clean failure. A scripted workload mixing scans, hot-key reuse, dirtying, and pin/unpin must agree with an independent oracle on every byte read back and on the exact eviction order.

Project: Build a buffer pool manager in Python that mediates all access to a fixed-size on- disk page file (pages are fixed-width byte arrays addressed by page id) through a bounded set of in-memory frames. The pool has a configurable capacity of N frames and a page table mapping resident page_id -> frame. Expose: `fetch_page(page_id)` which returns a pinned frame (reading from disk on miss, evicting if the pool is full), `new_page()` which allocates a fresh page id and a pinned zeroed frame, `unpin_page(page_id, is_dirty)` which decrements the pin count and ORs in the dirty flag, `flush_page(page_id)` and `flush_all()` which write dirty frames back to disk and clear the dirty flag, and `delete_page(page_id)`. Eviction MUST use the LRU-K replacement policy (default K=2): track the last K access timestamps per frame, never evict a frame whose pin count is > 0, choose the victim with the largest backward k-distance (frames with fewer than K recorded accesses are treated as having infinite k-distance and are evicted first, tie-broken by least- recent access), and write the victim back to disk before reuse if it is dirty. A `fetch_page` that cannot find an unpinned, evictable frame must fail explicitly rather than overflow the pool. Persist nothing beyond the page file itself; correctness is about the cache discipline. Acceptance: the resident page count never exceeds N; a page is never evicted while pinned; a dirty page is always written to disk before its frame is reused and reading it back returns the last unpinned contents (no lost update); when frames have full access history the chosen victim matches a reference LRU-K computation, and an access pattern that defeats plain LRU (e.g. a single large scan amid a hot working set) must NOT evict the hot set under LRU-K; and a fetch with all frames pinned returns a clean failure. A scripted workload mixing scans, hot-key reuse, dirtying, and pin/unpin must agree with an independent oracle on every byte read back and on the exact eviction order.

Project: Build a buffer pool manager in Python that mediates all access to a fixed-size on- disk page file (pages are fixed-width byte arrays addressed by page id) through a bounded set of in-memory frames. The pool has a configurable capacity of N frames and a page table mapping resident page_id -> frame. Expose: `fetch_page(page_id)` which returns a pinned frame (reading from disk on miss, evicting if the pool is full), `new_page()` which allocates a fresh page id and a pinned zeroed frame, `unpin_page(page_id, is_dirty)` which decrements the pin count and ORs in the dirty flag, `flush_page(page_id)` and `flush_all()` which write dirty frames back to disk and clear the dirty flag, and `delete_page(page_id)`. Eviction MUST use the LRU-K replacement policy (default K=2): track the last K access timestamps per frame, never evict a frame whose pin count is > 0, choose the victim with the largest backward k-distance (frames with fewer than K recorded accesses are treated as having infinite k-distance and are evicted first, tie-broken by least- recent access), and write the victim back to disk before reuse if it is dirty. A `fetch_page` that cannot find an unpinned, evictable frame must fail explicitly rather than overflow the pool. Persist nothing beyond the page file itself; correctness is about the cache discipline. Acceptance: the resident page count never exceeds N; a page is never evicted while pinned; a dirty page is always written to disk before its frame is reused and reading it back returns the last unpinned contents (no lost update); when frames have full access history the chosen victim matches a reference LRU-K computation, and an access pattern that defeats plain LRU (e.g. a single large scan amid a hot working set) must NOT evict the hot set under LRU-K; and a fetch with all frames pinned returns a clean failure. A scripted workload mixing scans, hot-key reuse, dirtying, and pin/unpin must agree with an independent oracle on every byte read back and on the exact eviction order.

"""
Simple CLI / demo entry point for the buffer pool manager.

The script reads a YAML configuration file (default: ``config.yaml``),
instantiates a :class:`~buffer_pool_manager.BufferPoolManager` with the
provided parameters, and exercises a small subset of its public API:

1. Allocate a new page.
2. Fetch the page data (pinning it).
3. Unpin the page while marking it dirty.
4. Flush the dirty page to disk.
5. Allocate a second page.
6. Delete the first page.
7. Flush all remaining pages and cleanly shut down.

Running the demo:

    $ python main.py               # uses ./config.yaml
    $ python main.py -c my.cfg     # specify an alternative config file
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import sys
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any, Dict

import yaml

from buffer_pool_manager import BufferPoolManager


def load_config(path: Path) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """
    Load the YAML configuration file.

    Parameters
    ----------
    path : Path
        Path to the ``config.yaml`` file.

    Returns
    -------
    dict
        Dictionary with keys ``page_file_path``, ``page_size``,
        ``pool_capacity`` and ``lru_k`` as required by the data contract.
    """
    if not path.is_file():
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"Configuration file not found: {path}")

    with path.open("r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        cfg = yaml.safe_load(f)

    required_keys = {"page_file_path", "page_size", "pool_capacity", "lru_k"}
    missing = required_keys - cfg.keys()
    if missing:
        raise KeyError(f"Configuration file is missing keys: {missing}")

    # Basic type validation (the manager will also validate)
    if not isinstance(cfg["page_file_path"], str):
        raise TypeError("page_file_path must be a string")
    if not isinstance(cfg["page_size"], int):
        raise TypeError("page_size must be an integer")
    if not isinstance(cfg["pool_capacity"], int):
        raise TypeError("pool_capacity must be an integer")
    if not isinstance(cfg["lru_k"], int):
        raise TypeError("lru_k must be an integer")

    return cfg


def demo_buffer_pool_manager(cfg: Dict[str, Any]) -> None:
    """
    Demonstrate a typical usage pattern of :class:`BufferPoolManager`.

    The function is deliberately linear and prints each step so that a user
    can follow what is happening.

    Parameters
    ----------
    cfg : dict
        Configuration dictionary as produced by :func:`load_config`.
    """

Project: Build a buffer pool manager in Python that mediates all access to a fixed-size on- disk page file (pages are fixed-width byte arrays addressed by page id) through a bounded set of in-memory frames. The pool has a configurable capacity of N frames and a page table mapping resident page_id -> frame. Expose: `fetch_page(page_id)` which returns a pinned frame (reading from disk on miss, evicting if the pool is full), `new_page()` which allocates a fresh page id and a pinned zeroed frame, `unpin_page(page_id, is_dirty)` which decrements the pin count and ORs in the dirty flag, `flush_page(page_id)` and `flush_all()` which write dirty frames back to disk and clear the dirty flag, and `delete_page(page_id)`. Eviction MUST use the LRU-K replacement policy (default K=2): track the last K access timestamps per frame, never evict a frame whose pin count is > 0, choose the victim with the largest backward k-distance (frames with fewer than K recorded accesses are treated as having infinite k-distance and are evicted first, tie-broken by least- recent access), and write the victim back to disk before reuse if it is dirty. A `fetch_page` that cannot find an unpinned, evictable frame must fail explicitly rather than overflow the pool. Persist nothing beyond the page file itself; correctness is about the cache discipline. Acceptance: the resident page count never exceeds N; a page is never evicted while pinned; a dirty page is always written to disk before its frame is reused and reading it back returns the last unpinned contents (no lost update); when frames have full access history the chosen victim matches a reference LRU-K computation, and an access pattern that defeats plain LRU (e.g. a single large scan amid a hot working set) must NOT evict the hot set under LRU-K; and a fetch with all frames pinned returns a clean failure. A scripted workload mixing scans, hot-key reuse, dirtying, and pin/unpin must agree with an independent oracle on every byte read back and on the exact eviction order.

"""
Buffer pool manager implementation.

Provides a public API for managing pages in memory with a fixed‑size
buffer pool, coordinating disk I/O via :class:`PageFile`, in‑memory
metadata via :class:`Frame`, and eviction via :class:`LRUKReplacer`.

Public API
~~~~~~~~~~
- fetch_page(page_id) -> bytes
- new_page() -> int
- unpin_page(page_id, is_dirty=False) -> None
- flush_page(page_id) -> None
- flush_all() -> None
- delete_page(page_id) -> None
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import threading
from typing import Dict

from page_file import PageFile
from frame import Frame
from lru_k import LRUKReplacer


class BufferPoolManager:
    """
    Manage a fixed‑size pool of in‑memory page frames.

    Parameters
    ----------
    page_file_path : str
        Path to the underlying page file.
    page_size : int
        Size of each page in bytes.
    pool_capacity : int
        Maximum number of pages that may reside in memory simultaneously.

        The *K* parameter for the LRU‑K replacement policy.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        page_file_path: str,
        page_size: int,
        pool_capacity: int,
        lru_k: int = 2,
    ) -> None:
        if page_size <= 0:
            raise ValueError("page_size must be positive")
        if pool_capacity <= 0:
            raise ValueError("pool_capacity must be positive")
        if lru_k <= 0:
            raise ValueError("lru_k must be positive")

        self._page_file = PageFile(page_file_path, page_size)
        self._page_size = page_size
        self._capacity = pool_capacity

        # Canonical state: mapping from page_id to its Frame object.
        self.page_table: Dict[int, Frame] = {}

        # In‑memory storage of the actual page bytes.  The dict mirrors
        # ``page_table`` keys; values are mutable ``bytearray`` objects of length
        # ``page_size``.
        self._pages_data: Dict[int, bytearray] = {}

        # Replacement policy works directly on ``page_table``.
        self._replacer = LRUKReplacer(self.page_table, k=lru_k)

        # Simple lock to make the manager thread‑safe (not required by spec but
        # cheap and safe).
        self._lock = threading.Lock()

        # Remember the most recent victim for external inspection (e.g. demos).
        self._last_evicted: int | None = None

    # --------------------------------------------------------------------- #
    # Helper utilities
    # --------------------------------------------------------------------- #

    def _is_full(self) -> bool:
        """Return True if the buffer pool already holds ``capacity`` frames."""
        return len(self.page_table) >= self._capacity

        """
        Evict a single frame according to the LRU‑K policy.

        ------

"""
In‑memory representation of a page frame.

The Frame object tracks:
* The page identifier it holds.
* A history of the most recent K access timestamps (oldest first).
* The current pin count – how many clients are using the page.
* Whether the page has been modified since it was last flushed (dirty flag).

All state fields follow the exact contracts required by the rest of the
system:

    Frame.access_times -> list[float]   (length ≤ K, oldest first)
    Frame.pin_count   -> int ≥ 0
    Frame.dirty       -> bool

The BufferPoolManager stores frames in its ``page_table`` as
``dict[int, Frame]`` mapping a page id to the corresponding Frame instance.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import time
from typing import List


class Frame:
    """
    Represents a single page frame held in the buffer pool.

    Parameters
    ----------
    page_id: int
        Identifier of the page stored in this frame.
    k: int
        Maximum number of recent access timestamps to retain for LRU‑K.
    """

    __slots__ = ("page_id", "k", "access_times", "pin_count", "dirty")

    def __init__(self, page_id: int, k: int) -> None:
        if k <= 0:
            raise ValueError("k must be a positive integer")
        self.page_id: int = page_id
        self.k: int = k
        # Canonical state – ordered oldest → newest, length ≤ k
        self.access_times: List[float] = []
        self.pin_count: int = 0  # ≥ 0
        self.dirty: bool = False

    # --------------------------------------------------------------------- #
    # Access‑time handling (LRU‑K)
    # --------------------------------------------------------------------- #
    def record_access(self, timestamp: float | None = None) -> None:
        """
        Record an access at ``timestamp``. If ``timestamp`` is omitted,
        the current time from :pyfunc:`time.time` is used.

        The timestamp is appended to ``access_times`` while preserving the
        contract that the list contains at most ``k`` entries, ordered
        from oldest to newest.
        """
        if timestamp is None:
            timestamp = time.time()
        # Append new access
        self.access_times.append(timestamp)
        # Trim excess oldest entries
        if len(self.access_times) > self.k:
            # Remove the oldest entry (index 0) until length ≤ k
            excess = len(self.access_times) - self.k
            del self.access_times[0:excess]

    def get_access_history(self) -> List[float]:
        """
        Return a shallow copy of the access‑time list.

        The returned list follows the canonical ordering (oldest first)
        and respects the length limit ``k``.
        """
        return list(self.access_times)

    # --------------------------------------------------------------------- #
    # Pin count management
    # --------------------------------------------------------------------- #
    def pin(self) -> None:
        """Increment the pin count, indicating an additional client is using the page."""
        self.pin_count += 1

    def unpin(self) -> None:
        """
        Decrement the pin count.

        Raises
        ------
        RuntimeError
            If an attempt is made to unpin a frame whose pin count is already zero.
        """
        if self.pin_count == 0:
            raise RuntimeError("Cannot unpin a frame with pin count 0")
        self.pin_count -= 1

    # --------------------------------------------------------------------- #
    # Dirty flag handling
    # --------------------------------------------------------------------- #
    def set_dirty(self, dirty: bool = True) -> None:
        """
        Set the dirty flag.

        Parameters
        ----------
        dirty: bool, optional
            ``True`` marks the frame as modified; ``False`` clears the flag.
            Defaults to ``True``.
        """
        self.dirty = dirty

    def is_dirty(self) -> bool:
        """Return the current state of the dirty flag."""
        return self.dirty

    # --------------------------------------------------------------------- #
    # Utility / representation
    # --------------------------------------------------------------------- #
    def __repr__(self) -> str:
        return (
            f"Frame(page_id={self.page_id}, pin_count={self.pin_count}, "
            f"dirty={self.dirty}, access_times={self.access_times})"
        )

Project: Build a buffer pool manager in Python that mediates all access to a fixed-size on- disk page file (pages are fixed-width byte arrays addressed by page id) through a bounded set of in-memory frames. The pool has a configurable capacity of N frames and a page table mapping resident page_id -> frame. Expose: `fetch_page(page_id)` which returns a pinned frame (reading from disk on miss, evicting if the pool is full), `new_page()` which allocates a fresh page id and a pinned zeroed frame, `unpin_page(page_id, is_dirty)` which decrements the pin count and ORs in the dirty flag, `flush_page(page_id)` and `flush_all()` which write dirty frames back to disk and clear the dirty flag, and `delete_page(page_id)`. Eviction MUST use the LRU-K replacement policy (default K=2): track the last K access timestamps per frame, never evict a frame whose pin count is > 0, choose the victim with the largest backward k-distance (frames with fewer than K recorded accesses are treated as having infinite k-distance and are evicted first, tie-broken by least- recent access), and write the victim back to disk before reuse if it is dirty. A `fetch_page` that cannot find an unpinned, evictable frame must fail explicitly rather than overflow the pool. Persist nothing beyond the page file itself; correctness is about the cache discipline. Acceptance: the resident page count never exceeds N; a page is never evicted while pinned; a dirty page is always written to disk before its frame is reused and reading it back returns the last unpinned contents (no lost update); when frames have full access history the chosen victim matches a reference LRU-K computation, and an access pattern that defeats plain LRU (e.g. a single large scan amid a hot working set) must NOT evict the hot set under LRU-K; and a fetch with all frames pinned returns a clean failure. A scripted workload mixing scans, hot-key reuse, dirtying, and pin/unpin must agree with an independent oracle on every byte read back and on the exact eviction order.

Project: Build a buffer pool manager in Python that mediates all access to a fixed-size on- disk page file (pages are fixed-width byte arrays addressed by page id) through a bounded set of in-memory frames. The pool has a configurable capacity of N frames and a page table mapping resident page_id -> frame. Expose: `fetch_page(page_id)` which returns a pinned frame (reading from disk on miss, evicting if the pool is full), `new_page()` which allocates a fresh page id and a pinned zeroed frame, `unpin_page(page_id, is_dirty)` which decrements the pin count and ORs in the dirty flag, `flush_page(page_id)` and `flush_all()` which write dirty frames back to disk and clear the dirty flag, and `delete_page(page_id)`. Eviction MUST use the LRU-K replacement policy (default K=2): track the last K access timestamps per frame, never evict a frame whose pin count is > 0, choose the victim with the largest backward k-distance (frames with fewer than K recorded accesses are treated as having infinite k-distance and are evicted first, tie-broken by least- recent access), and write the victim back to disk before reuse if it is dirty. A `fetch_page` that cannot find an unpinned, evictable frame must fail explicitly rather than overflow the pool. Persist nothing beyond the page file itself; correctness is about the cache discipline. Acceptance: the resident page count never exceeds N; a page is never evicted while pinned; a dirty page is always written to disk before its frame is reused and reading it back returns the last unpinned contents (no lost update); when frames have full access history the chosen victim matches a reference LRU-K computation, and an access pattern that defeats plain LRU (e.g. a single large scan amid a hot working set) must NOT evict the hot set under LRU-K; and a fetch with all frames pinned returns a clean failure. A scripted workload mixing scans, hot-key reuse, dirtying, and pin/unpin must agree with an independent oracle on every byte read back and on the exact eviction order.

    if not isinstance(cfg["page_size"], int):

    if not isinstance(cfg["pool_capacity"], int):

    1. Create a ``BufferPoolManager`` instance using the supplied configuration.
    2. Allocate pages up to the configured ``pool_capacity``.
    3. Access each allocated page a distinct number of times so that their
       LRU‑K histories differ (the first page is accessed once, the second
       twice, …).  This establishes a deterministic ordering for the LRU‑K
       replacer.

       the manager must evict a victim according to the LRU‑K policy.
    5. Print the identifier of the evicted page so that the test harness can

    all pages are unpinned (and marked dirty) before the final allocation,
    ensuring that eviction is possible.

"""
Simple CLI / demo entry point for the buffer pool manager.

The script reads a YAML configuration file (default: ``config.yaml``),
instantiates a :class:`~buffer_pool_manager.BufferPoolManager` with the
provided parameters, and provides an interactive REPL for manual testing.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import sys
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any, Dict

import yaml

from buffer_pool_manager import BufferPoolManager


def load_config(path: Path) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """Load the YAML configuration file.

    Parameters
    ----------
    path : Path
        Path to the ``config.yaml`` file.

    Returns
    -------
    dict
        Dictionary with keys ``page_file_path``, ``page_size``,
        ``pool_capacity`` and ``lru_k`` as required by the data contract.
    """
    if not path.is_file():
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"Configuration file not found: {path}")

    with path.open("r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        cfg = yaml.safe_load(f)

    required_keys = {"page_file_path", "page_size", "pool_capacity", "lru_k"}
    missing = required_keys - cfg.keys()
    if missing:
        raise KeyError(f"Configuration file is missing keys: {missing}")

    return cfg


def _interactive_cli(bpm: BufferPoolManager) -> None:
    """Simple REPL for manual testing of the buffer pool manager.

    Supported commands (space‑separated arguments):
        new_page                     – allocate a new page and pin it
        fetch_page <id>              – fetch (and pin) an existing page
        unpin_page <id> [dirty]      – unpin the page; optional ``dirty`` flag
        delete_page <id>             – delete a page from the pool/file
        flush_page <id>              – flush a specific page to disk
        flush_all                    – flush all dirty pages
        exit / quit                  – leave the REPL
    """
    help_msg = (
        "Commands: new_page, fetch_page <id>, unpin_page <id> [dirty], delete_page <id>, "
        "flush_page <id>, flush_all, exit, quit, help"
    )
    print("=== Interactive BufferPoolManager session ===")
    print(help_msg)
    while True:
        try:
            line = input("> ")
        except EOFError:
            break
        if not line:
            continue
        parts = line.strip().split()
        cmd, *args = parts
        try:
            if cmd == "new_page":
                new_id, evicted = bpm.new_page()
                print(f"Allocated page {new_id}{' (evicted ' + str(evicted) + ')' if evicted else ''}")
            elif cmd == "fetch_page":
                if len(args) != 1:
                    print("Usage: fetch_page <id>")
                    continue
                pid = int(args[0])
                _ = bpm.fetch_page(pid)
                print(f"Fetched page {pid}")
            elif cmd == "unpin_page":
                if len(args) < 1:
                    print("Usage: unpin_page <id> [dirty]")
                    continue
                pid = int(args[0])
                is_dirty = len(args) > 1 and args[1].lower() in {"dirty", "true", "1"}
                bpm.unpin_page(pid, is_dirty=is_dirty)
                print(f"Unpinned page {pid}{' (dirty)' if is_dirty else ''}")
            elif cmd == "delete_page":
                if len(args) != 1:
                    print("Usage: delete_page <id>")
                    continue
                pid = int(args[0])
                bpm.delete_page(pid)
                print(f"Deleted page {pid}")
            elif cmd == "flush_page":
                if len(args) != 1:
                    print("Usage: flush_page <id>")
                    continue
                pid = int(args[0])
                bpm.flush_page(pid)
                print(f"Flushed page {pid}")
            elif cmd == "flush_all":
                bpm.flush_all()
                print("Flushed all dirty pages")
            elif cmd in {"exit", "quit"}:
                break
            elif cmd == "help":
                print(help_msg)
            else:
                print(f"Unknown command: {cmd}. Type 'help' for usage.")
        except Exception as exc:
            print(f"Error: {exc}")
    print("=== Interactive session terminated ===")


def build_arg_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Interactive BufferPoolManager CLI")
    parser.add_argument(
        "-c",
        "--config",
        type=Path,
        default=Path("config.yaml"),
        help="Path to the YAML configuration file (default: config.yaml)",
    )
    return parser


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    """Entry point for the script.

    Returns
    -------
    int
        Exit status code (0 for success, non‑zero for failure).
    """
    parser = build_arg_parser()
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    try:
        cfg = load_config(args.config)
        with BufferPoolManager(
            page_file_path=cfg["page_file_path"],
            page_size=cfg["page_size"],
            pool_capacity=cfg["pool_capacity"],
            lru_k=cfg["lru_k"],
        ) as bpm:
            _interactive_cli(bpm)
        return 0
    except Exception as exc:  # pragma: no cover – top‑level error handling
        print(f"Error: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

"""
Simple CLI / demo entry point for the buffer pool manager.

The script reads a YAML configuration file (default: ``config.yaml``),
instantiates a :class:`~buffer_pool_manager.BufferPoolManager` with the
provided parameters, and provides an interactive REPL for manual testing.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import sys
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any, Dict

import yaml

from buffer_pool_manager import BufferPoolManager


def load_config(path: Path) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """Load the YAML configuration file.

    Parameters
    ----------
    path : Path
        Path to the ``config.yaml`` file.

    Returns
    -------
    dict
        Dictionary with keys ``page_file_path``, ``page_size``,
        ``pool_capacity`` and ``lru_k`` as required by the data contract.
    """
    if not path.is_file():
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"Configuration file not found: {path}")

    with path.open("r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        cfg = yaml.safe_load(f)

    required_keys = {"page_file_path", "page_size", "pool_capacity", "lru_k"}
    missing = required_keys - cfg.keys()
    if missing:
        raise KeyError(f"Configuration file is missing keys: {missing}")

    return cfg


def _interactive_cli(bpm: BufferPoolManager) -> None:
    """Simple REPL for manual testing of the buffer pool manager.

    Supported commands (space‑separated arguments):
        new_page                     – allocate a new page and pin it
        fetch_page <id>              – fetch (and pin) an existing page
        unpin_page <id> [dirty]      – unpin the page; optional ``dirty`` flag
        delete_page <id>             – delete a page from the pool/file
        flush_page <id>              – flush a specific page to disk
        flush_all                    – flush all dirty pages
        exit / quit                  – leave the REPL
    """
    help_msg = (
        "Commands: new_page, fetch_page <id>, unpin_page <id> [dirty], delete_page <id>, "
        "flush_page <id>, flush_all, exit, quit, help"
    )
    print("=== Interactive BufferPoolManager session ===")
    print(help_msg)
    while True:
        try:
            line = input("> ")
        except EOFError:
            break
        if not line:
            continue
        parts = line.strip().split()
        cmd, *args = parts
        try:
            if cmd == "new_page":
                new_id, evicted = bpm.new_page()
                print(f"Allocated page {new_id}{' (evicted ' + str(evicted) + ')' if evicted else ''}")
            elif cmd == "fetch_page":
                if len(args) != 1:
                    print("Usage: fetch_page <id>")
                    continue
                pid = int(args[0])
                _ = bpm.fetch_page(pid)
                print(f"Fetched page {pid}")
            elif cmd == "unpin_page":
                if len(args) < 1:
                    print("Usage: unpin_page <id> [dirty]")
                    continue
                pid = int(args[0])
                is_dirty = len(args) > 1 and args[1].lower() in {"dirty", "true", "1"}
                bpm.unpin_page(pid, is_dirty=is_dirty)
                print(f"Unpinned page {pid}{' (dirty)' if is_dirty else ''}")
            elif cmd == "delete_page":
                if len(args) != 1:
                    print("Usage: delete_page <id>")
                    continue
                pid = int(args[0])
                bpm.delete_page(pid)
                print(f"Deleted page {pid}")
            elif cmd == "flush_page":
                if len(args) != 1:
                    print("Usage: flush_page <id>")
                    continue
                pid = int(args[0])
                bpm.flush_page(pid)
                print(f"Flushed page {pid}")
            elif cmd == "flush_all":
                bpm.flush_all()
                print("Flushed all dirty pages")
            elif cmd in {"exit", "quit"}:
                break
            elif cmd == "help":
                print(help_msg)
            else:
                print(f"Unknown command: {cmd}. Type 'help' for usage.")
        except Exception as exc:
            print(f"Error: {exc}")
    print("=== Interactive session terminated ===")


def build_arg_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Interactive BufferPoolManager CLI")
    parser.add_argument(
        "-c",
        "--config",
        type=Path,
        default=Path("config.yaml"),
        help="Path to the YAML configuration file (default: config.yaml)",
    )
    return parser


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    """Entry point for the script.

    Returns
    -------
    int
        Exit status code (0 for success, non‑zero for failure).
    """
    parser = build_arg_parser()
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    try:
        cfg = load_config(args.config)
        with BufferPoolManager(
            page_file_path=cfg["page_file_path"],
            page_size=cfg["page_size"],
            pool_capacity=cfg["pool_capacity"],
            lru_k=cfg["lru_k"],
        ) as bpm:
            _interactive_cli(bpm)
        return 0
    except Exception as exc:  # pragma: no cover – top‑level error handling
        print(f"Error: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

- flush_page(page_id) -> None
- flush_all() -> None
- delete_page(page_id) -> None

class BufferPoolManager:
    """
    Manage a fixed‑size pool of in‑memory page frames.

    Parameters
    ----------
    page_file_path : str
        Path to the underlying page file.
    page_size : int
        Size of each page in bytes.
    pool_capacity : int
        Maximum number of pages that may reside in memory simultaneously.

        The *K* parameter for the LRU‑K replacement policy.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        page_file_path: str,
        page_size: int,
        pool_capacity: int,
        lru_k: int = 2,
    ) -> None:
        if page_size <= 0:
            raise ValueError("page_size must be positive")
        if pool_capacity <= 0:
            raise ValueError("pool_capacity must be positive")
        if lru_k <= 0:
            raise ValueError("lru_k must be positive")

        self._page_file = PageFile(page_file_path, page_size)
        self._page_size = page_size
        self._capacity = pool_capacity

        # Canonical state: mapping from page_id to its Frame object.
        self.page_table: Dict[int, Frame] = {}

        # In‑memory storage of the actual page bytes.  The dict mirrors
        # ``page_table`` keys; values are mutable ``bytearray`` objects of length
        # ``page_size``.
        self._pages_data: Dict[int, bytearray] = {}

        # Replacement policy works directly on ``page_table``.
        self._replacer = LRUKReplacer(self.page_table, k=lru_k)

        # Simple lock to make the manager thread‑safe (not required by spec but
        # cheap and safe).
        self._lock = threading.Lock()

        # Remember the most recent victim for external inspection (e.g. demos).
        self._last_evicted: int | None = None

    # --------------------------------------------------------------------- #
    # Helper utilities
    # --------------------------------------------------------------------- #

    def _is_full(self) -> bool:
        """Return True if the buffer pool already holds ``capacity`` frames."""
        return len(self.page_table) >= self._capacity

        Evict a single frame according to the LRU‑K policy.

        RuntimeError
            If no evictable frame exists (all frames are pinned).

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse

from pathlib import Path

def load_config(path: Path) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """Load the YAML configuration file.

    Parameters
    ----------
    path : Path
        Path to the ``config.yaml`` file.

    Returns
    -------
    dict
        Dictionary with keys ``page_file_path``, ``page_size``,
        ``pool_capacity`` and ``lru_k`` as required by the data contract.
    """
    if not path.is_file():
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"Configuration file not found: {path}")

    with path.open("r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        cfg = yaml.safe_load(f)

    required_keys = {"page_file_path", "page_size", "pool_capacity", "lru_k"}
    missing = required_keys - cfg.keys()
    if missing:
        raise KeyError(f"Configuration file is missing keys: {missing}")

    return cfg

                if len(args) != 1:

def build_arg_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:

        type=Path,
        default=Path("config.yaml"),

    def unpin_page(self, page_id: int, is_dirty: bool = False) -> None:
        """
        Decrease the pin count of ``page_id``. Optionally mark it dirty.

        Parameters
        ----------
        page_id : int

        """

            if frame.is_dirty():

                self._page_file.write_page(page_id, data_bytes)

        with self._lock:

                    self._page_file.write_page(page_id, data_bytes)

    required_keys = {"page_file_path", "page_size", "pool_capacity", "lru_k"}
    missing = required_keys - cfg.keys()
    if missing:
        raise KeyError(f"Configuration file is missing keys: {missing}")

def load_config(path: Path) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """Load the YAML configuration file.

    Parameters
    ----------

    Returns

    if not path.is_file():
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"Configuration file not found: {path}")

    with path.open("r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        cfg = yaml.safe_load(f)

    required_keys = {"page_file_path", "page_size", "pool_capacity", "lru_k"}
    missing = required_keys - cfg.keys()
    if missing:
        raise KeyError(f"Configuration file is missing keys: {missing}")

    return cfg

                pid = int(args[0])
                is_dirty = len(args) > 1 and args[1].lower() in {"dirty", "true", "1"}
                bpm.unpin_page(pid, is_dirty=is_dirty)

                if len(args) != 1:
                    print("Usage: delete_page <id>")

                pid = int(args[0])
                bpm.delete_page(pid)
                print(f"Deleted page {pid}")

                if len(args) != 1:
                    print("Usage: flush_page <id>")

                bpm.flush_page(pid)

def build_arg_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:

        "-c",
        "--config",
        type=Path,
        default=Path("config.yaml"),
        help="Path to the YAML configuration file (default: config.yaml)",

def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:

    except Exception as exc:  # pragma: no cover – top‑level error handling

"""
Simple CLI / demo entry point for the buffer pool manager.

The script reads a YAML configuration file (default: ``config.yaml``),
instantiates a :class:`~buffer_pool_manager.BufferPoolManager` with the
provided parameters, and provides an interactive REPL for manual testing.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import sys
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any, Dict

import yaml

from buffer_pool_manager import BufferPoolManager


def load_config(path: Path) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """Load the YAML configuration file.

    Parameters
    ----------
    path : Path
        Path to the ``config.yaml`` file.

    Returns
    -------
    dict
        Dictionary with keys ``page_file_path``, ``page_size``,
        ``pool_capacity`` and ``lru_k`` as required by the data contract.
    """
    if not path.is_file():
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"Configuration file not found: {path}")

    with path.open("r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        cfg = yaml.safe_load(f)

    required_keys = {"page_file_path", "page_size", "pool_capacity", "lru_k"}
    missing = required_keys - cfg.keys()
    if missing:
        raise KeyError(f"Configuration file is missing keys: {missing}")

    return cfg


def _interactive_cli(bpm: BufferPoolManager) -> None:
    """Simple REPL for manual testing of the buffer pool manager.

    Supported commands (space‑separated arguments):
        new_page                     – allocate a new page and pin it
        fetch_page <id>              – fetch (and pin) an existing page
        unpin_page <id> [dirty]      – unpin the page; optional ``dirty`` flag
        delete_page <id>             – delete a page from the pool/file
        flush_page <id>              – flush a specific page to disk
        flush_all                    – flush all dirty pages
        exit / quit                  – leave the REPL
    """
    help_msg = (
        "Commands: new_page, fetch_page <id>, unpin_page <id> [dirty], delete_page <id>, "
        "flush_page <id>, flush_all, exit, quit, help"
    )
    print("=== Interactive BufferPoolManager session ===")
    print(help_msg)
    while True:
        try:
            line = input("> ")
        except EOFError:
            break
        if not line:
            continue
        parts = line.strip().split()
        cmd, *args = parts
        try:
            if cmd == "new_page":
                new_id, evicted = bpm.new_page()
                print(f"Allocated page {new_id}{' (evicted ' + str(evicted) + ')' if evicted else ''}")
            elif cmd == "fetch_page":
                if len(args) != 1:
                    print("Usage: fetch_page <id>")
                    continue
                pid = int(args[0])
                _ = bpm.fetch_page(pid)
                print(f"Fetched page {pid}")
            elif cmd == "unpin_page":
                if len(args) < 1:
                    print("Usage: unpin_page <id> [dirty]")
                    continue
                pid = int(args[0])
                is_dirty = len(args) > 1 and args[1].lower() in {"dirty", "true", "1"}
                bpm.unpin_page(pid, is_dirty=is_dirty)
                print(f"Unpinned page {pid}{' (dirty)' if is_dirty else ''}")
            elif cmd == "delete_page":
                if len(args) != 1:
                    print("Usage: delete_page <id>")
                    continue
                pid = int(args[0])
                bpm.delete_page(pid)
                print(f"Deleted page {pid}")
            elif cmd == "flush_page":
                if len(args) != 1:
                    print("Usage: flush_page <id>")
                    continue
                pid = int(args[0])
                bpm.flush_page(pid)
                print(f"Flushed page {pid}")
            elif cmd == "flush_all":
                bpm.flush_all()
                print("Flushed all dirty pages")
            elif cmd in {"exit", "quit"}:
                break
            elif cmd == "help":
                print(help_msg)
            else:
                print(f"Unknown command: {cmd}. Type 'help' for usage.")
        except Exception as exc:
            print(f"Error: {exc}")
    print("=== Interactive session terminated ===")


def build_arg_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Interactive BufferPoolManager CLI")
    parser.add_argument(
        "-c",
        "--config",
        type=Path,
        default=Path("config.yaml"),
        help="Path to the YAML configuration file (default: config.yaml)",
    )
    return parser


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    """Entry point for the script.

    Returns
    -------
    int
        Exit status code (0 for success, non‑zero for failure).
    """
    parser = build_arg_parser()
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    try:
        cfg = load_config(args.config)
        with BufferPoolManager(
            page_file_path=cfg["page_file_path"],
            page_size=cfg["page_size"],
            pool_capacity=cfg["pool_capacity"],
            lru_k=cfg["lru_k"],
        ) as bpm:
            _interactive_cli(bpm)
        return 0
    except Exception as exc:  # pragma: no cover – top‑level error handling
        print(f"Error: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import sys
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any, Dict

import yaml

from buffer_pool_manager import BufferPoolManager


def load_config(path: Path) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """Load the YAML configuration file.

    Parameters
    ----------
    path : Path
        Path to the ``config.yaml`` file.

    Returns
    -------
    dict
        Dictionary with keys ``page_file_path``, ``page_size``,
        ``pool_capacity`` and ``lru_k`` as required by the data contract.
    """
    if not path.is_file():
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"Configuration file not found: {path}")

    with path.open("r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        cfg = yaml.safe_load(f)

    required_keys = {"page_file_path", "page_size", "pool_capacity", "lru_k"}
    missing = required_keys - cfg.keys()
    if missing:
        raise KeyError(f"Configuration file is missing keys: {missing}")

    return cfg


def _interactive_cli(bpm: BufferPoolManager) -> None:
    """Simple REPL for manual testing of the buffer pool manager.

    Supported commands (space‑separated arguments):
        new_page                     – allocate a new page and pin it
        fetch_page <id>              – fetch (and pin) an existing page
        unpin_page <id> [dirty]      – unpin the page; optional ``dirty`` flag
        delete_page <id>             – delete a page from the pool/file
        flush_page <id>              – flush a specific page to disk
        flush_all                    – flush all dirty pages
        exit / quit                  – leave the REPL
    """
    help_msg = (
        "Commands: new_page, fetch_page <id>, unpin_page <id> [dirty], delete_page <id>, "
        "flush_page <id>, flush_all, exit, quit, help"
    )
    print("=== Interactive BufferPoolManager session ===")

    while True:
        try:
            line = input("> ")
        except EOFError:

        if not line:

        try:

                print(f"Allocated page {new_id}{' (evicted ' + str(evicted) + ')' if evicted else ''}")

                if len(args) != 1:
                    print("Usage: fetch_page <id>")
                    continue
                pid = int(args[0])
                _ = bpm.fetch_page(pid)
                print(f"Fetched page {pid}")

                if len(args) < 1:
                    print("Usage: unpin_page <id> [dirty]")
                    continue
                pid = int(args[0])
                is_dirty = len(args) > 1 and args[1].lower() in {"dirty", "true", "1"}
                bpm.unpin_page(pid, is_dirty=is_dirty)
                print(f"Unpinned page {pid}{' (dirty)' if is_dirty else ''}")
            elif cmd == "delete_page":
                if len(args) != 1:
                    print("Usage: delete_page <id>")
                    continue
                pid = int(args[0])
                bpm.delete_page(pid)
                print(f"Deleted page {pid}")
            elif cmd == "flush_page":
                if len(args) != 1:
                    print("Usage: flush_page <id>")
                    continue
                pid = int(args[0])
                bpm.flush_page(pid)
                print(f"Flushed page {pid}")
            elif cmd == "flush_all":
                bpm.flush_all()
                print("Flushed all dirty pages")

                break
            elif cmd == "help":
                print(help_msg)
            else:
                print(f"Unknown command: {cmd}. Type 'help' for usage.")
        except Exception as exc:
            print(f"Error: {exc}")
    print("=== Interactive session terminated ===")


def build_arg_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Interactive BufferPoolManager CLI")
    parser.add_argument(
        "-c",
        "--config",
        type=Path,
        default=Path("config.yaml"),
        help="Path to the YAML configuration file (default: config.yaml)",
    )
    return parser


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    """Entry point for the script.

    Returns
    -------
    int
        Exit status code (0 for success, non‑zero for failure).
    """
    parser = build_arg_parser()
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    try:
        cfg = load_config(args.config)
        with BufferPoolManager(
            page_file_path=cfg["page_file_path"],
            page_size=cfg["page_size"],
            pool_capacity=cfg["pool_capacity"],
            lru_k=cfg["lru_k"],
        ) as bpm:
            _interactive_cli(bpm)
        return 0
    except Exception as exc:  # pragma: no cover – top‑level error handling
        print(f"Error: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import sys
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any, Dict

import yaml

from buffer_pool_manager import BufferPoolManager


def load_config(path: Path) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """Load the YAML configuration file.

    Parameters
    ----------
    path : Path
        Path to the ``config.yaml`` file.

    Returns
    -------
    dict
        Dictionary with keys ``page_file_path``, ``page_size``,
        ``pool_capacity`` and ``lru_k`` as required by the data contract.
    """
    if not path.is_file():
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"Configuration file not found: {path}")

    with path.open("r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        cfg = yaml.safe_load(f)

    required_keys = {"page_file_path", "page_size", "pool_capacity", "lru_k"}
    missing = required_keys - cfg.keys()
    if missing:
        raise KeyError(f"Configuration file is missing keys: {missing}")

    return cfg


def _interactive_cli(bpm: BufferPoolManager) -> None:
    """Simple REPL for manual testing of the buffer pool manager.

    Supported commands (space‑separated arguments):
        new_page                     – allocate a new page and pin it
        fetch_page <id>              – fetch (and pin) an existing page
        unpin_page <id> [dirty]      – unpin the page; optional ``dirty`` flag
        delete_page <id>             – delete a page from the pool/file
        flush_page <id>              – flush a specific page to disk
        flush_all                    – flush all dirty pages
        exit / quit                  – leave the REPL
    """
    help_msg = (
        "Commands: new_page, fetch_page <id>, unpin_page <id> [dirty], delete_page <id>, "
        "flush_page <id>, flush_all, exit, quit, help"
    )
    print("=== Interactive BufferPoolManager session ===")
    print(help_msg)
    while True:
        try:
            line = input("> ")
        except EOFError:
            break
        if not line:
            continue
        parts = line.strip().split()
        cmd, *args = parts
        try:
            if cmd == "new_page":
                new_id, evicted = bpm.new_page()
                print(f"Allocated page {new_id}{' (evicted ' + str(evicted) + ')' if evicted else ''}")
            elif cmd == "fetch_page":
                if len(args) != 1:
                    print("Usage: fetch_page <id>")
                    continue
                pid = int(args[0])
                _ = bpm.fetch_page(pid)
                print(f"Fetched page {pid}")
            elif cmd == "unpin_page":
                if len(args) < 1:
                    print("Usage: unpin_page <id> [dirty]")
                    continue
                pid = int(args[0])
                is_dirty = len(args) > 1 and args[1].lower() in {"dirty", "true", "1"}
                bpm.unpin_page(pid, is_dirty=is_dirty)
                print(f"Unpinned page {pid}{' (dirty)' if is_dirty else ''}")
            elif cmd == "delete_page":
                if len(args) != 1:
                    print("Usage: delete_page <id>")
                    continue
                pid = int(args[0])
                bpm.delete_page(pid)
                print(f"Deleted page {pid}")
            elif cmd == "flush_page":
                if len(args) != 1:
                    print("Usage: flush_page <id>")
                    continue
                pid = int(args[0])
                bpm.flush_page(pid)
                print(f"Flushed page {pid}")
            elif cmd == "flush_all":
                bpm.flush_all()
                print("Flushed all dirty pages")
            elif cmd in {"exit", "quit"}:
                break
            elif cmd == "help":
                print(help_msg)
            else:
                print(f"Unknown command: {cmd}. Type 'help' for usage.")
        except Exception as exc:
            print(f"Error: {exc}")
    print("=== Interactive session terminated ===")


def build_arg_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Interactive BufferPoolManager CLI")
    parser.add_argument(
        "-c",
        "--config",
        type=Path,
        default=Path("config.yaml"),
        help="Path to the YAML configuration file (default: config.yaml)",
    )
    return parser


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    """Entry point for the script.

    Returns
    -------
    int
        Exit status code (0 for success, non‑zero for failure).
    """
    parser = build_arg_parser()
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    try:
        cfg = load_config(args.config)
        with BufferPoolManager(
            page_file_path=cfg["page_file_path"],
            page_size=cfg["page_size"],
            pool_capacity=cfg["pool_capacity"],
            lru_k=cfg["lru_k"],
        ) as bpm:
            _interactive_cli(bpm)
        return 0
    except Exception as exc:  # pragma: no cover – top‑level error handling
        print(f"Error: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Any, Dict

import yaml

def load_config(path: Path) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """Load the YAML configuration file.

    Parameters
    ----------
    path : Path
        Path to the ``config.yaml`` file.

    Returns
    -------
    dict
        Dictionary with keys ``page_file_path``, ``page_size``,

    """
    if not path.is_file():

    with path.open("r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        cfg = yaml.safe_load(f)

    required_keys = {"page_file_path", "page_size", "pool_capacity", "lru_k"}
    missing = required_keys - cfg.keys()
    if missing:
        raise KeyError(f"Configuration file is missing keys: {missing}")

    return cfg


def _interactive_cli(bpm: BufferPoolManager) -> None:
    """Simple REPL for manual testing of the buffer pool manager.

                    print("Usage: fetch_page <id>")

                pid = int(args[0])
                _ = bpm.fetch_page(pid)
                print(f"Fetched page {pid}")

                if len(args) < 1:
                    print("Usage: unpin_page <id> [dirty]")
                    continue
                pid = int(args[0])
                is_dirty = len(args) > 1 and args[1].lower() in {"dirty", "true", "1"}
                bpm.unpin_page(pid, is_dirty=is_dirty)
                print(f"Unpinned page {pid}{' (dirty)' if is_dirty else ''}")

                if len(args) != 1:
                    print("Usage: delete_page <id>")
                    continue
                pid = int(args[0])
                bpm.delete_page(pid)
                print(f"Deleted page {pid}")

                if len(args) != 1:
                    print("Usage: flush_page <id>")
                    continue
                pid = int(args[0])
                bpm.flush_page(pid)
                print(f"Flushed page {pid}")

                bpm.flush_all()
                print("Flushed all dirty pages")

                break

            print(f"Error: {exc}")
    print("=== Interactive session terminated ===")


def build_arg_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Interactive BufferPoolManager CLI")
    parser.add_argument(
        "-c",
        "--config",
        type=Path,
        default=Path("config.yaml"),
        help="Path to the YAML configuration file (default: config.yaml)",
    )
    return parser


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    """Entry point for the script.

    Returns
    -------
    int
        Exit status code (0 for success, non‑zero for failure).
    """
    parser = build_arg_parser()
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    try:

            page_size=cfg["page_size"],
            pool_capacity=cfg["pool_capacity"],
            lru_k=cfg["lru_k"],
        ) as bpm:
            _interactive_cli(bpm)
        return 0
    except Exception as exc:  # pragma: no cover – top‑level error handling
        print(f"Error: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

Project: Build a buffer pool manager in Python that mediates all access to a fixed-size on- disk page file (pages are fixed-width byte arrays addressed by page id) through a bounded set of in-memory frames. The pool has a configurable capacity of N frames and a page table mapping resident page_id -> frame. Expose: `fetch_page(page_id)` which returns a pinned frame (reading from disk on miss, evicting if the pool is full), `new_page()` which allocates a fresh page id and a pinned zeroed frame, `unpin_page(page_id, is_dirty)` which decrements the pin count and ORs in the dirty flag, `flush_page(page_id)` and `flush_all()` which write dirty frames back to disk and clear the dirty flag, and `delete_page(page_id)`. Eviction MUST use the LRU-K replacement policy (default K=2): track the last K access timestamps per frame, never evict a frame whose pin count is > 0, choose the victim with the largest backward k-distance (frames with fewer than K recorded accesses are treated as having infinite k-distance and are evicted first, tie-broken by least- recent access), and write the victim back to disk before reuse if it is dirty. A `fetch_page` that cannot find an unpinned, evictable frame must fail explicitly rather than overflow the pool. Persist nothing beyond the page file itself; correctness is about the cache discipline. Acceptance: the resident page count never exceeds N; a page is never evicted while pinned; a dirty page is always written to disk before its frame is reused and reading it back returns the last unpinned contents (no lost update); when frames have full access history the chosen victim matches a reference LRU-K computation, and an access pattern that defeats plain LRU (e.g. a single large scan amid a hot working set) must NOT evict the hot set under LRU-K; and a fetch with all frames pinned returns a clean failure. A scripted workload mixing scans, hot-key reuse, dirtying, and pin/unpin must agree with an independent oracle on every byte read back and on the exact eviction order.

"""
Simple CLI / demo entry point for the buffer pool manager.

The script reads a YAML configuration file (default: ``config.yaml``),
instantiates a :class:`~buffer_pool_manager.BufferPoolManager` with the
provided parameters, and provides an interactive REPL for manual testing.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import sys
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any, Dict

import yaml

from buffer_pool_manager import BufferPoolManager


def load_config(path: Path) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """Load the YAML configuration file.

    Parameters
    ----------
    path : Path
        Path to the ``config.yaml`` file.

    Returns
    -------
    dict
        Dictionary with keys ``page_file_path``, ``page_size``,
        ``pool_capacity`` and ``lru_k`` as required by the data contract.
    """
    if not path.is_file():
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"Configuration file not found: {path}")

    with path.open("r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        cfg = yaml.safe_load(f)

    required_keys = {"page_file_path", "page_size", "pool_capacity", "lru_k"}
    missing = required_keys - cfg.keys()
    if missing:
        raise KeyError(f"Configuration file is missing keys: {missing}")

    return cfg


def _interactive_cli(bpm: BufferPoolManager) -> None:
    """Simple REPL for manual testing of the buffer pool manager.

    Supported commands (space‑separated arguments):
        new_page                     – allocate a new page and pin it
        fetch_page <id>              – fetch (and pin) an existing page
        unpin_page <id> [dirty]      – unpin the page; optional ``dirty`` flag
        delete_page <id>             – delete a page from the pool/file
        flush_page <id>              – flush a specific page to disk
        flush_all                    – flush all dirty pages
        exit / quit                  – leave the REPL
    """
    help_msg = (
        "Commands: new_page, fetch_page <id>, unpin_page <id> [dirty], delete_page <id>, "
        "flush_page <id>, flush_all, exit, quit, help"
    )
    print("=== Interactive BufferPoolManager session ===")
    print(help_msg)
    while True:
        try:
            line = input("> ")
        except EOFError:
            break
        if not line:
            continue
        parts = line.strip().split()
        cmd, *args = parts
        try:
            if cmd == "new_page":
                new_id, evicted = bpm.new_page()
                print(f"Allocated page {new_id}{' (evicted ' + str(evicted) + ')' if evicted else ''}")
            elif cmd == "fetch_page":
                if len(args) != 1:
                    print("Usage: fetch_page <id>")
                    continue
                pid = int(args[0])
                _ = bpm.fetch_page(pid)
                print(f"Fetched page {pid}")
            elif cmd == "unpin_page":
                if len(args) < 1:
                    print("Usage: unpin_page <id> [dirty]")
                    continue
                pid = int(args[0])
                is_dirty = len(args) > 1 and args[1].lower() in {"dirty", "true", "1"}
                bpm.unpin_page(pid, is_dirty=is_dirty)
                print(f"Unpinned page {pid}{' (dirty)' if is_dirty else ''}")
            elif cmd == "delete_page":
                if len(args) != 1:
                    print("Usage: delete_page <id>")
                    continue
                pid = int(args[0])
                bpm.delete_page(pid)
                print(f"Deleted page {pid}")
            elif cmd == "flush_page":
                if len(args) != 1:
                    print("Usage: flush_page <id>")
                    continue
                pid = int(args[0])
                bpm.flush_page(pid)
                print(f"Flushed page {pid}")
            elif cmd == "flush_all":
                bpm.flush_all()
                print("Flushed all dirty pages")
            elif cmd in {"exit", "quit"}:
                break
            elif cmd == "help":
                print(help_msg)
            else:
                print(f"Unknown command: {cmd}. Type 'help' for usage.")
        except Exception as exc:
            print(f"Error: {exc}")
    print("=== Interactive session terminated ===")


def build_arg_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Interactive BufferPoolManager CLI")
    parser.add_argument(
        "-c",
        "--config",
        type=Path,
        default=Path("config.yaml"),
        help="Path to the YAML configuration file (default: config.yaml)",

def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:

Project: Build a buffer pool manager in Python that mediates all access to a fixed-size on- disk page file (pages are fixed-width byte arrays addressed by page id) through a bounded set of in-memory frames. The pool has a configurable capacity of N frames and a page table mapping resident page_id -> frame. Expose: `fetch_page(page_id)` which returns a pinned frame (reading from disk on miss, evicting if the pool is full), `new_page()` which allocates a fresh page id and a pinned zeroed frame, `unpin_page(page_id, is_dirty)` which decrements the pin count and ORs in the dirty flag, `flush_page(page_id)` and `flush_all()` which write dirty frames back to disk and clear the dirty flag, and `delete_page(page_id)`. Eviction MUST use the LRU-K replacement policy (default K=2): track the last K access timestamps per frame, never evict a frame whose pin count is > 0, choose the victim with the largest backward k-distance (frames with fewer than K recorded accesses are treated as having infinite k-distance and are evicted first, tie-broken by least- recent access), and write the victim back to disk before reuse if it is dirty. A `fetch_page` that cannot find an unpinned, evictable frame must fail explicitly rather than overflow the pool. Persist nothing beyond the page file itself; correctness is about the cache discipline. Acceptance: the resident page count never exceeds N; a page is never evicted while pinned; a dirty page is always written to disk before its frame is reused and reading it back returns the last unpinned contents (no lost update); when frames have full access history the chosen victim matches a reference LRU-K computation, and an access pattern that defeats plain LRU (e.g. a single large scan amid a hot working set) must NOT evict the hot set under LRU-K; and a fetch with all frames pinned returns a clean failure. A scripted workload mixing scans, hot-key reuse, dirtying, and pin/unpin must agree with an independent oracle on every byte read back and on the exact eviction order.
