Project: Build a persistent log-structured-merge key-value store in Python over a single data directory. Writes go to a write-ahead log (append a length-prefixed record, fsync) and an in-memory sorted memtable; when the memtable exceeds a configurable size threshold (e.g. 4MB or N keys) it is frozen and flushed to an immutable on- disk SSTable at level 0, after which the corresponding WAL segment may be retired. Each SSTable stores keys in sorted order with a sparse block index in its footer and a per-table bloom filter sized for a target false-positive rate (<= 1%); deletes are tombstone records, not in-place removals. A `get(key)` checks the memtable, then any immutable memtables, then SSTables newest-to-oldest, consulting each table's bloom filter before touching disk and stopping at the first hit (including a tombstone, which reads as absent). Implement leveled compaction: level 0 may hold overlapping tables but triggers compaction at a fan-out limit, and levels >=1 hold non-overlapping key ranges with a size ratio (e.g. 10x) between levels; compaction merges overlapping tables into the next level, keeps only the newest value per key, and drops tombstones once no older level can contain the key. Provide an API/CLI: `put(k,v)`, `get(k)`, `delete(k)`, `scan(lo,hi)` (merged sorted iteration across all levels honoring tombstones and version precedence), `flush()`, `compact()`, plus `open(dir)`/`close()`. Crash recovery on `open` must replay surviving WAL segments to rebuild the memtable and load existing SSTable metadata so no acknowledged write is lost. Acceptance: 50000 mixed put/delete/get ops must match a dict oracle on every get and on a full scan; bloom filters must never report a false negative; after a simulated crash (process exit without clean close) reopening recovers every fsynced write; after compaction the on-disk level invariants (L0 fan-out bound, non-overlapping ranges and size ratios at L>=1) must hold and stale versions/obsolete tombstones must be physically gone.

Project: Build a persistent log-structured-merge key-value store in Python over a single data directory. Writes go to a write-ahead log (append a length-prefixed record, fsync) and an in-memory sorted memtable; when the memtable exceeds a configurable size threshold (e.g. 4MB or N keys) it is frozen and flushed to an immutable on- disk SSTable at level 0, after which the corresponding WAL segment may be retired. Each SSTable stores keys in sorted order with a sparse block index in its footer and a per-table bloom filter sized for a target false-positive rate (<= 1%); deletes are tombstone records, not in-place removals. A `get(key)` checks the memtable, then any immutable memtables, then SSTables newest-to-oldest, consulting each table's bloom filter before touching disk and stopping at the first hit (including a tombstone, which reads as absent). Implement leveled compaction: level 0 may hold overlapping tables but triggers compaction at a fan-out limit, and levels >=1 hold non-overlapping key ranges with a size ratio (e.g. 10x) between levels; compaction merges overlapping tables into the next level, keeps only the newest value per key, and drops tombstones once no older level can contain the key. Provide an API/CLI: `put(k,v)`, `get(k)`, `delete(k)`, `scan(lo,hi)` (merged sorted iteration across all levels honoring tombstones and version precedence), `flush()`, `compact()`, plus `open(dir)`/`close()`. Crash recovery on `open` must replay surviving WAL segments to rebuild the memtable and load existing SSTable metadata so no acknowledged write is lost. Acceptance: 50000 mixed put/delete/get ops must match a dict oracle on every get and on a full scan; bloom filters must never report a false negative; after a simulated crash (process exit without clean close) reopening recovers every fsynced write; after compaction the on-disk level invariants (L0 fan-out bound, non-overlapping ranges and size ratios at L>=1) must hold and stale versions/obsolete tombstones must be physically gone.

Project: Build a persistent log-structured-merge key-value store in Python over a single data directory. Writes go to a write-ahead log (append a length-prefixed record, fsync) and an in-memory sorted memtable; when the memtable exceeds a configurable size threshold (e.g. 4MB or N keys) it is frozen and flushed to an immutable on- disk SSTable at level 0, after which the corresponding WAL segment may be retired. Each SSTable stores keys in sorted order with a sparse block index in its footer and a per-table bloom filter sized for a target false-positive rate (<= 1%); deletes are tombstone records, not in-place removals. A `get(key)` checks the memtable, then any immutable memtables, then SSTables newest-to-oldest, consulting each table's bloom filter before touching disk and stopping at the first hit (including a tombstone, which reads as absent). Implement leveled compaction: level 0 may hold overlapping tables but triggers compaction at a fan-out limit, and levels >=1 hold non-overlapping key ranges with a size ratio (e.g. 10x) between levels; compaction merges overlapping tables into the next level, keeps only the newest value per key, and drops tombstones once no older level can contain the key. Provide an API/CLI: `put(k,v)`, `get(k)`, `delete(k)`, `scan(lo,hi)` (merged sorted iteration across all levels honoring tombstones and version precedence), `flush()`, `compact()`, plus `open(dir)`/`close()`. Crash recovery on `open` must replay surviving WAL segments to rebuild the memtable and load existing SSTable metadata so no acknowledged write is lost. Acceptance: 50000 mixed put/delete/get ops must match a dict oracle on every get and on a full scan; bloom filters must never report a false negative; after a simulated crash (process exit without clean close) reopening recovers every fsynced write; after compaction the on-disk level invariants (L0 fan-out bound, non-overlapping ranges and size ratios at L>=1) must hold and stale versions/obsolete tombstones must be physically gone.

Project: Build a persistent log-structured-merge key-value store in Python over a single data directory. Writes go to a write-ahead log (append a length-prefixed record, fsync) and an in-memory sorted memtable; when the memtable exceeds a configurable size threshold (e.g. 4MB or N keys) it is frozen and flushed to an immutable on- disk SSTable at level 0, after which the corresponding WAL segment may be retired. Each SSTable stores keys in sorted order with a sparse block index in its footer and a per-table bloom filter sized for a target false-positive rate (<= 1%); deletes are tombstone records, not in-place removals. A `get(key)` checks the memtable, then any immutable memtables, then SSTables newest-to-oldest, consulting each table's bloom filter before touching disk and stopping at the first hit (including a tombstone, which reads as absent). Implement leveled compaction: level 0 may hold overlapping tables but triggers compaction at a fan-out limit, and levels >=1 hold non-overlapping key ranges with a size ratio (e.g. 10x) between levels; compaction merges overlapping tables into the next level, keeps only the newest value per key, and drops tombstones once no older level can contain the key. Provide an API/CLI: `put(k,v)`, `get(k)`, `delete(k)`, `scan(lo,hi)` (merged sorted iteration across all levels honoring tombstones and version precedence), `flush()`, `compact()`, plus `open(dir)`/`close()`. Crash recovery on `open` must replay surviving WAL segments to rebuild the memtable and load existing SSTable metadata so no acknowledged write is lost. Acceptance: 50000 mixed put/delete/get ops must match a dict oracle on every get and on a full scan; bloom filters must never report a false negative; after a simulated crash (process exit without clean close) reopening recovers every fsynced write; after compaction the on-disk level invariants (L0 fan-out bound, non-overlapping ranges and size ratios at L>=1) must hold and stale versions/obsolete tombstones must be physically gone.

"""
Simple REPL / CLI for interacting with the KVStore.

Supported commands (case‑insensitive):
    PUT <key> <value>   – Store the value under the given key.
    GET <key>           – Retrieve the value for the given key.
    EXIT | QUIT         – Shut down the store and terminate the program.

All keys and values are treated as UTF‑8 strings and converted to ``bytes``
before being handed to :class:`kvstore.KVStore`.  Errors from the store are
propagated to the user as plain text messages.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import sys
from typing import Optional

# Import KVStore directly from the store module to avoid executing the
# package's ``__init__`` (which may import this CLI and cause a circular import).
from .store import KVStore


def _print(msg: str) -> None:
    """Write a message to stdout with a trailing newline and flush."""
    sys.stdout.write(msg + "\n")
    sys.stdout.flush()


def _handle_put(store: KVStore, args: list[str]) -> None:

    Execute a PUT command.

    Expected ``args`` layout: [key, value]
    """
    if len(args) < 2:
        _print("ERROR: PUT requires a key and a value")
        return

    key_str, value_str = args[0], " ".join(args[1:])
    try:
        store.put(key_str.encode("utf-8"), value_str.encode("utf-8"))
        _print("OK")
    except Exception as exc:  # pragma: no cover – defensive
        _print(f"ERROR: {exc}")


def _handle_get(store: KVStore, args: list[str]) -> None:
    """
    Execute a GET command.

    Expected ``args`` layout: [key]
    """
    if len(args) != 1:
        _print("ERROR: GET requires exactly one key")
        return

    key_str = args[0]
    try:
        result: Optional[bytes] = store.get(key_str.encode("utf-8"))
        if result is None:
            _print("NULL")
        else:
            # Decode using UTF‑8; fall back to repr if decoding fails.
            try:
                _print(result.decode("utf-8"))
            except UnicodeDecodeError:
                _print(repr(result))
    except Exception as exc:  # pragma: no cover – defensive
        _print(f"ERROR: {exc}")


def _dispatch_command(store: KVStore, line: str) -> bool:
    """
    Parse and execute a single command line.

    Returns ``True`` if the REPL should continue, ``False`` to exit.
    """
    # Ignore empty input lines
    if not line:
        return True

    parts = line.split()
    cmd = parts[0].upper()
    args = parts[1:]

    if cmd == "PUT":
        _handle_put(store, args)
    elif cmd == "GET":
        _handle_get(store, args)
    elif cmd in ("DELETE", "DEL"):
        _handle_delete(store, args)
    elif cmd == "SCAN":
        _handle_scan(store, args)
    elif cmd == "COMPACT":
        # Perform compaction and acknowledge success
        store.compact()
        _print("OK")
    elif cmd in ("EXIT", "QUIT"):
        return False
    else:
        _print(f"ERROR: unknown command '{cmd}'")
    return True


def main_cli() -> None:
    """
    Entry point for the KVStore command‑line interface.

    Usage (via ``python -m kvstore.cli`` or through ``main.py``):
        python main.py [data_dir]

    ``data_dir`` is passed to :class:`kvstore.KVStore`.  If omitted,
    the current working directory is used.
    """
    # Determine the data directory – either the first CLI argument or "."
    data_dir = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "."

    try:
        store = KVStore(data_dir)
    except Exception as exc:  # pragma: no cover – defensive
        _print(f"Failed to open KVStore at '{data_dir}': {exc}")
        sys.exit(1)

    _print("KVStore REPL. Type PUT, GET, or EXIT.")
    try:
        while True:
            # Prompt without interfering with redirected input streams.
            _print("> ")
            line = sys.stdin.readline()
            if not line:  # EOF
                break
            continue_loop = _dispatch_command(store, line.strip())
            if not continue_loop:

Project: Build a persistent log-structured-merge key-value store in Python over a single data directory. Writes go to a write-ahead log (append a length-prefixed record, fsync) and an in-memory sorted memtable; when the memtable exceeds a configurable size threshold (e.g. 4MB or N keys) it is frozen and flushed to an immutable on- disk SSTable at level 0, after which the corresponding WAL segment may be retired. Each SSTable stores keys in sorted order with a sparse block index in its footer and a per-table bloom filter sized for a target false-positive rate (<= 1%); deletes are tombstone records, not in-place removals. A `get(key)` checks the memtable, then any immutable memtables, then SSTables newest-to-oldest, consulting each table's bloom filter before touching disk and stopping at the first hit (including a tombstone, which reads as absent). Implement leveled compaction: level 0 may hold overlapping tables but triggers compaction at a fan-out limit, and levels >=1 hold non-overlapping key ranges with a size ratio (e.g. 10x) between levels; compaction merges overlapping tables into the next level, keeps only the newest value per key, and drops tombstones once no older level can contain the key. Provide an API/CLI: `put(k,v)`, `get(k)`, `delete(k)`, `scan(lo,hi)` (merged sorted iteration across all levels honoring tombstones and version precedence), `flush()`, `compact()`, plus `open(dir)`/`close()`. Crash recovery on `open` must replay surviving WAL segments to rebuild the memtable and load existing SSTable metadata so no acknowledged write is lost. Acceptance: 50000 mixed put/delete/get ops must match a dict oracle on every get and on a full scan; bloom filters must never report a false negative; after a simulated crash (process exit without clean close) reopening recovers every fsynced write; after compaction the on-disk level invariants (L0 fan-out bound, non-overlapping ranges and size ratios at L>=1) must hold and stale versions/obsolete tombstones must be physically gone.

Project: Build a persistent log-structured-merge key-value store in Python over a single data directory. Writes go to a write-ahead log (append a length-prefixed record, fsync) and an in-memory sorted memtable; when the memtable exceeds a configurable size threshold (e.g. 4MB or N keys) it is frozen and flushed to an immutable on- disk SSTable at level 0, after which the corresponding WAL segment may be retired. Each SSTable stores keys in sorted order with a sparse block index in its footer and a per-table bloom filter sized for a target false-positive rate (<= 1%); deletes are tombstone records, not in-place removals. A `get(key)` checks the memtable, then any immutable memtables, then SSTables newest-to-oldest, consulting each table's bloom filter before touching disk and stopping at the first hit (including a tombstone, which reads as absent). Implement leveled compaction: level 0 may hold overlapping tables but triggers compaction at a fan-out limit, and levels >=1 hold non-overlapping key ranges with a size ratio (e.g. 10x) between levels; compaction merges overlapping tables into the next level, keeps only the newest value per key, and drops tombstones once no older level can contain the key. Provide an API/CLI: `put(k,v)`, `get(k)`, `delete(k)`, `scan(lo,hi)` (merged sorted iteration across all levels honoring tombstones and version precedence), `flush()`, `compact()`, plus `open(dir)`/`close()`. Crash recovery on `open` must replay surviving WAL segments to rebuild the memtable and load existing SSTable metadata so no acknowledged write is lost. Acceptance: 50000 mixed put/delete/get ops must match a dict oracle on every get and on a full scan; bloom filters must never report a false negative; after a simulated crash (process exit without clean close) reopening recovers every fsynced write; after compaction the on-disk level invariants (L0 fan-out bound, non-overlapping ranges and size ratios at L>=1) must hold and stale versions/obsolete tombstones must be physically gone.

        self.sstable_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

        if not isinstance(key, (bytes, bytearray)):

        if not isinstance(value, (bytes, bytearray)):

def _encode_varint(value: int) -> bytes:
    """Encode an integer as unsigned LEB128."""
    if value < 0:
        raise ValueError("varint cannot be negative")
    out = bytearray()
    while True:
        to_write = value & 0x7F
        value >>= 7
        if value:
            out.append(to_write | 0x80)
        else:
            out.append(to_write)
            break
    return bytes(out)


def _decode_varint(data: bytes, offset: int = 0) -> Tuple[int, int]:
    """Decode an unsigned LEB128 from data starting at offset.
    Returns (value, new_offset)."""
    shift = 0
    result = 0
    pos = offset
    while True:
        if pos >= len(data):
            raise EOFError("Unexpected end of data while reading varint")
        byte = data[pos]
        result |= (byte & 0x7F) << shift
        pos += 1
        if not (byte & 0x80):

        shift += 7

class BloomFilter:
    """Simple Bloom filter with deterministic SHA‑256 based hash functions."""

    _MAGIC = b"BFIL"  # 4‑byte identifier for sanity checks

    def __init__(self, capacity: int, fpr: float):
        if capacity <= 0:
            raise ValueError("capacity must be > 0")
        if not (0 < fpr < 1):
            raise ValueError("fpr must be between 0 and 1")

        # optimal size in bits
        m = -capacity * math.log(fpr) / (math.log(2) ** 2)
        self.num_bits = int(m)
        self.num_bytes = (self.num_bits + 7) // 8
        self.k = max(1, int(round((self.num_bits / capacity) * math.log(2))))

        self._bits = bytearray(self.num_bytes)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Hash helpers
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def _hashes(self, key: bytes) -> List[int]:
        """Generate k hash values for the given key."""
        digest = hashlib.sha256(key).digest()
        hashes = []
        needed = self.k
        i = 0
        while needed > 0:
            start = (i * 4) % len(digest)
            chunk = digest[start : start + 4]
            if len(chunk) < 4:
                chunk += digest[: 4 - len(chunk)]
            hv = struct.unpack("<I", chunk)[0]
            hashes.append(hv)
            i += 1
            needed -= 1
        return hashes

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Public API
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def add(self, key: bytes) -> None:
        for hv in self._hashes(key):
            bit_pos = hv % self.num_bits
            byte_idx = bit_pos // 8
            mask = 1 << (bit_pos % 8)
            self._bits[byte_idx] |= mask

    def might_contain(self, key: bytes) -> bool:
        for hv in self._hashes(key):
            bit_pos = hv % self.num_bits
            byte_idx = bit_pos // 8
            mask = 1 << (bit_pos % 8)
            if not (self._bits[byte_idx] & mask):
                return False
        return True

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Serialization
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def serialize(self) -> bytes:
        """Serialize to: [magic][num_bits:uint32][k:uint32][bits...]"""
        header = self._MAGIC + struct.pack("<II", self.num_bits, self.k)
        return header + bytes(self._bits)

    def deserialize(cls, data: bytes) -> "BloomFilter":
        """Deserialize from the format produced by `serialize`."""
        if len(data) < 4 + 8:

        magic = data[:4]

        obj.num_bits = num_bits
        obj.k = k
        obj._bits = bits
        obj.num_bytes = (num_bits + 7) // 8

Project: Build a persistent log-structured-merge key-value store in Python over a single data directory. Writes go to a write-ahead log (append a length-prefixed record, fsync) and an in-memory sorted memtable; when the memtable exceeds a configurable size threshold (e.g. 4MB or N keys) it is frozen and flushed to an immutable on- disk SSTable at level 0, after which the corresponding WAL segment may be retired. Each SSTable stores keys in sorted order with a sparse block index in its footer and a per-table bloom filter sized for a target false-positive rate (<= 1%); deletes are tombstone records, not in-place removals. A `get(key)` checks the memtable, then any immutable memtables, then SSTables newest-to-oldest, consulting each table's bloom filter before touching disk and stopping at the first hit (including a tombstone, which reads as absent). Project: Build a persistent log-structured-merge key-value store in Python over a single data directory. Writes go to a write-ahead log (append a length-prefixed record, fsync) and an in-memory sorted memtable; when the memtable exceeds a configurable size threshold (e.g. 4MB or N keys) it is frozen and flushed to an immutable on- disk SSTable at level 0, after which the corresponding WAL segment may be retired. Each SSTable stores keys in sorted order with a sparse block index in its footer and a per-table bloom filter sized for a target false-positive rate (<= 1%); deletes are tombstone records, not in-place removals. A `get(key)` checks the memtable, then any immutable memtables, then SSTables newest-to-oldest, consulting each table's bloom filter before touching disk and stopping at the first hit (including a tombstone, which reads as absent). Implement leveled compaction: level 0 may hold overlapping tables but triggers compaction at a fan-out limit, and levels >=1 hold non-overlapping key ranges with a size ratio (e.g. 10x) between levels; compaction merges overlapping tables into the next level, keeps only the newest value per key, and drops tombstones once no older level can contain the key. Provide an API/CLI: `put(k,v)`, `get(k)`, `delete(k)`, `scan(lo,hi)` (merged sorted iteration across all levels honoring tombstones and version precedence), `flush()`, `compact()`, plus `open(dir)`/`close()`. Crash recovery on `open` must replay surviving WAL segments to rebuild the memtable and load existing SSTable metadata so no acknowledged write is lost. Acceptance: 50000 mixed put/delete/get ops must match a dict oracle on every get and on a full scan; bloom filters must never report a false negative; after a simulated crash (process exit without clean close) reopening recovers every fsynced write; after compaction the on-disk level invariants (L0 fan-out bound, non-overlapping ranges and size ratios at L>=1) must hold and stale versions/obsolete tombstones must be physically gone.

Project: Build a persistent log-structured-merge key-value store in Python over a single data directory. Writes go to a write-ahead log (append a length-prefixed record, fsync) and an in-memory sorted memtable; when the memtable exceeds a configurable size threshold (e.g. 4MB or N keys) it is frozen and flushed to an immutable on- disk SSTable at level 0, after which the corresponding WAL segment may be retired. Each SSTable stores keys in sorted order with a sparse block index in its footer and a per-table bloom filter sized for a target false-positive rate (<= 1%); deletes are tombstone records, not in-place removals. A `get(key)` checks the memtable, then any immutable memtables, then SSTables newest-to-oldest, consulting each table's bloom filter before touching disk and stopping at the first hit (including a tombstone, which reads as absent). Implement leveled compaction: level 0 may hold overlapping tables but triggers compaction at a fan-out limit, and levels >=1 hold non-overlapping key ranges with a size ratio (e.g. 10x) between levels; compaction merges overlapping tables into the next level, keeps only the newest value per key, and drops tombstones once no older level can contain the key. Provide an API/CLI: `put(k,v)`, `get(k)`, `delete(k)`, `scan(lo,hi)` (merged sorted iteration across all levels honoring tombstones and version precedence), `flush()`, `compact()`, plus `open(dir)`/`close()`. Crash recovery on `open` must replay surviving WAL segments to rebuild the memtable and load existing SSTable metadata so no acknowledged write is lost. Acceptance: 50000 mixed put/delete/get ops must match a dict oracle on every get and on a full scan; bloom filters must never report a false negative; after a simulated crash (process exit without clean close) reopening recovers every fsynced write; after compaction the on-disk level invariants (L0 fan-out bound, non-overlapping ranges and size ratios at L>=1) must hold and stale versions/obsolete tombstones must be physically gone.

Project: Build an expression compiler in Python that turns infix arithmetic/boolean expressions into a textual stack-machine assembly program, plus an assembler and a tiny stack VM that runs it, exposed as `exprc compile '<expr>'` (print assembly), `exprc run '<expr>'` (compile + execute, print result), and `exprc asm <file.s>` (assemble + run a hand-written assembly file). """
Command‑line interface for the ExprC language.

Provides three sub‑commands:

* ``compile`` – Parse a source file and compile it to an instruction list.
* ``asm``     – Assemble raw assembly source into an instruction list.
* ``run``     – Parse, compile and execute an expression, printing the result.

All errors are reported on stderr with a non‑zero exit status.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import sys
from pathlib import Path
from typing import List, Tuple, Any

# Fixed imports: reference concrete sub‑modules directly.
from exprc.parser import Parser, ParseError
from exprc.compiler import Compiler, CompileError
from exprc.assembler import Assembler, AssemblyError
from exprc.vm import VirtualMachine, RuntimeError


def _handle_compile(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    """Handle the ``compile`` sub‑command.

    Reads the source file, parses it, compiles it and prints the resulting
    instruction list to stdout. Returns an exit code (0 on success).
    """
    try:
        source_path = Path(args.source)
        source_text = source_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        program = Parser.parse(source_text)  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
        instructions: List[Tuple[Any, Any]] = Compiler.compile(program)  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
        for instr in instructions:
            print(instr)
        return 0
    except FileNotFoundError as exc:
        sys.stderr.write(f"File not found: {exc.filename}\n")
        return 1
    except ParseError as exc:
        sys.stderr.write(f"Parse error: {exc}\n")
        return 2
    except CompileError as exc:
        sys.stderr.write(f"Compile error: {exc}\n")
        return 3


def _handle_asm(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    """Handle the ``asm`` sub‑command.

    Reads an assembly source file, assembles it into an instruction list and
    prints the list to stdout.
    """
    try:
        asm_path = Path(args.source)
        asm_text = asm_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        instructions: List[Tuple[Any, Any]] = Assembler.assemble(asm_text)  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
        for instr in instructions:
            print(instr)
        return 0
    except FileNotFoundError as exc:
        sys.stderr.write(f"File not found: {exc.filename}\n")
        return 1
    except AssemblyError as exc:
        sys.stderr.write(f"Assembly error: {exc}\n")
        return 2


def _handle_run(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    """Handle the ``run`` sub‑command.

    Parses the supplied expression string, compiles it, executes it on the
    virtual machine and prints the resulting value.
    """
    try:
        # ``args.expr`` may be quoted by the shell; we treat it as a raw string.
        program = Parser.parse(args.expr)  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
        instructions: List[Tuple[Any, Any]] = Compiler.compile(program)  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
        vm = VirtualMachine()
        result = vm.run(instructions)  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
        print(result)
        return 0
    except ParseError as exc:
        sys.stderr.write(f"Parse error: {exc}\n")
        return 1
    except CompileError as exc:
        sys.stderr.write(f"Compile error: {exc}\n")
        return 2
    except RuntimeError as exc:
        sys.stderr.write(f"Runtime error: {exc}\n")
        return 3


def build_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
    """Construct the top‑level argument parser with sub‑commands."""
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        prog="exprc", description="ExprC command‑line interface"
    )
    subparsers = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)

    # compile sub‑command
    compile_parser = subparsers.add_parser(
        "compile", help="Parse and compile a source file to an instruction list."
    )
    compile_parser.add_argument(
        "source", metavar="SOURCE", help="Path to the ExprC source file."
    )
    compile_parser.set_defaults(func=_handle_compile)

    # asm sub‑command
    asm_parser = subparsers.add_parser(
        "asm", help="Assemble raw assembly source into an instruction list."
    )
    asm_parser.add_argument(
        "source", metavar="SOURCE", help="Path to the assembly source file."
    )
    asm_parser.set_defaults(func=_handle_asm)

    # run sub‑command
    run_parser = subparsers.add_parser(
        "run", help="Parse, compile and execute an expression."
    )
    run_parser.add_argument(
        "expr", metavar="EXPR", help="Expression string to evaluate."
    )
    run_parser.set_defaults(func=_handle_run)

    return parser


def main(argv: List[str] | None = None) -> None:
    """Entry point for the ``python -m exprc`` command.

    Parses arguments, dispatches to the appropriate handler and exits with
    the handler's return code.
    """
    parser = build_parser()
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)

    # Each sub‑command handler returns an integer exit status.
    exit_code = args.func(args)  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
    sys.exit(exit_code)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

Project: Build an expression compiler in Python that turns infix arithmetic/boolean expressions into a textual stack-machine assembly program, plus an assembler and a tiny stack VM that runs it, exposed as `exprc compile '<expr>'` (print assembly), `exprc run '<expr>'` (compile + execute, print result), and `exprc asm <file.s>` (assemble + run a hand-written assembly file). Parse the surface language with a Pratt / precedence-climbing parser (you must implement precedence and associativity explicitly via binding powers, NOT defer to Python's `eval`): support `+ - * / %`, unary minus, comparison `== != < <= > >=`, `&&` `||` and `!`, parentheses, numeric literals, named variables, and `let <name> = <expr>;` bindings followed by a final expression; precedence from lowest to highest must be `||` < `&&` < comparison < additive < multiplicative < unary < primary, with `-`/`+`/`*`/`/`/`%` left-associative and unary right-associative, and the parser must reject malformed input (mismatched parens, a binary operator with a missing operand, an unknown token) with the column position. Define an EXPLICIT stack ISA as a documented set of mnemonics — e.g. PUSH <const>, LOAD <var>, STORE <var>, ADD, SUB, MUL, DIV, MOD, NEG, EQ, NE, LT, LE, GT, GE, AND, OR, NOT, and HALT — and lower the AST to a linear instruction list in correct evaluation order (post-order emission so operands are on the stack before each operator). Implement an assembler that parses the textual assembly into encoded instructions (resolving variable names to a slot table / symbol table) and a VM that executes them on an operand stack with a variable store, reporting runtime errors for stack underflow, division/modulo by zero, and an unknown mnemonic. Required edge cases and diagnostics: division and modulo by zero are runtime errors with a clear message; reading a variable that was never bound is a compile-time error; deeply nested and mixed-precedence expressions must lower correctly; and both the compiler and the hand-written-assembly path must reject unknown instructions/operands. Acceptance: the compiled output of an expression evaluates to the same value as a trusted reference evaluator across a battery of mixed-precedence and associativity cases (e.g. `2 - 3 - 4` = -5 confirms left-associativity, `2 + 3 * 4` = 14, `(2 + 3) * 4` = 20, `!(1 < 2) || 0` and short-circuit-free boolean arithmetic); the emitted instruction sequence is in valid post-order so the VM's stack has exactly one value (the result) at HALT for every well-formed program (assert final stack depth == 1); `let`-bound variables are stored and reloaded via STORE/LOAD with a stable slot assignment; and a hand-authored `.s` file assembles and runs to the expected result, with malformed assembly rejected rather than crashing.

"""AST node definitions for the ExprC language.

The compiler, assembler and VM work with these concrete syntax‑tree
objects.  All nodes are immutable dataclasses; they expose their
children via a ``children`` property to simplify visitor implementations.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import List, Tuple, Union

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Base type for all AST nodes – useful for type‑checking and visitors.
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
ASTNode = Union[
    "Literal",
    "Variable",
    "UnaryOp",
    "BinaryOp",
    "LetStmt",
    "Program",
]

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Literal values
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
Scalar = Union[int, float, bool]


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class Literal:
    """A scalar literal (int, float or bool)."""

    value: Scalar

    def __repr__(self) -> str:
        return f"Literal({self.value!r})"

    @property
    def children(self) -> Tuple[()]:
        """Literals have no child nodes."""
        return ()


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Variable reference
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class Variable:
    """Reference to a variable by name."""

    name: str

    def __repr__(self) -> str:
        return f"Variable({self.name!r})"

    @property
    def children(self) -> Tuple[()]:
        """Variables have no child nodes."""
        return ()


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Unary operation
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class UnaryOp:
    """Unary operator applied to a single operand.

    ``op`` is the textual representation used by the parser
    (e.g. '-', '!', '+').
    """

    op: str
    operand: ASTNode

def _handle_run(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    """Handle the ``run`` sub‑command.

    Parses the supplied expression string, compiles it, executes it on the
    virtual machine and prints the resulting value.

    try:

        instructions: List[Tuple[Any, Any]] = Compiler().compile(program)  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
        vm = VirtualMachine()
        result = vm.run(instructions)  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
        print(result)
        return 0
    except ParseError as exc:
        sys.stderr.write(f"Parse error: {exc}\n")
        return 1
    except CompileError as exc:
        sys.stderr.write(f"Compile error: {exc}\n")
        return 2
    except RuntimeError as exc:
        sys.stderr.write(f"Runtime error: {exc}\n")
        return 3

Project: Build an expression compiler in Python that turns infix arithmetic/boolean expressions into a textual stack-machine assembly program, plus an assembler and a tiny stack VM that runs it, exposed as `exprc compile '<expr>'` (print assembly), `exprc run '<expr>'` (compile + execute, print result), and `exprc asm <file.s>` (assemble + run a hand-written assembly file). Parse the surface language with a Pratt / precedence-climbing parser (you must implement precedence and associativity explicitly via binding powers, NOT defer to Python's `eval`): support `+ - * / %`, unary minus, comparison `== != < <= > >=`, `&&` `||` and `!`, parentheses, numeric literals, named variables, and `let <name> = <expr>;` bindings followed by a final expression; precedence from lowest to highest must be `||` < `&&` < comparison < additive < multiplicative < unary < primary, with `-`/`+`/`*`/`/`/`%` left-associative and unary right-associative, and the parser must reject malformed input (mismatched parens, a binary operator with a missing operand, an unknown token) with the column position. Define an EXPLICIT stack ISA as a documented set of mnemonics — e.g. PUSH <const>, LOAD <var>, STORE <var>, ADD, SUB, MUL, DIV, MOD, NEG, EQ, NE, LT, LE, GT, GE, AND, OR, NOT, and HALT — and lower the AST to a linear instruction list in correct evaluation order (post-order emission so operands are on the stack before each operator). Implement an assembler that parses the textual assembly into encoded instructions (resolving variable names to a slot table / symbol table) and a VM that executes them on an operand stack with a variable store, reporting runtime errors for stack underflow, division/modulo by zero, and an unknown mnemonic. Required edge cases and diagnostics: division and modulo by zero are runtime errors with a clear message; reading a variable that was never bound is a compile-time error; deeply nested and mixed-precedence expressions must lower correctly; and both the compiler and the hand-written-assembly path must reject unknown instructions/operands. Acceptance: the compiled output of an expression evaluates to the same value as a trusted reference evaluator across a battery of mixed-precedence and associativity cases (e.g. `2 - 3 - 4` = -5 confirms left-associativity, `2 + 3 * 4` = 14, `(2 + 3) * 4` = 20, `!(1 < 2) || 0` and short-circuit-free boolean arithmetic); the emitted instruction sequence is in valid post-order so the VM's stack has exactly one value (the result) at HALT for every well-formed program (assert final stack depth == 1); `let`-bound variables are stored and reloaded via STORE/LOAD with a stable slot assignment; and a hand-authored `.s` file assembles and runs to the expected result, with malformed assembly rejected rather than crashing.

"""
Compiler for the exprc language.

Transforms an abstract syntax tree (AST) into a linear list of assembly
mnemonics suitable for the assembler / virtual machine.

The compilation strategy is **post‑order emission**:
sub‑expressions are compiled first, then the operator that combines them.
Let‑bindings allocate slots in a variable table and use STORE/LOAD to
persist values across the program.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Any, List, Tuple

# AST node classes and program container
# NOTE: These symbols live in ``exprc.ast``; importing directly from the
# package root caused an ImportError because ``exprc.__init__`` does not
# re‑export them.
from exprc.ast import (
    Program,
    LetStmt,
    Variable,
    Literal,
    UnaryOp,
    BinaryOp,
)

# Mnemonic constants – each is emitted as a tuple (Mnemonic, operand?)
# NOTE: Mnemonics are defined in ``exprc.instructions``. Importing from the
# package root fails for the same reason as above.
from exprc.instructions import (
    PUSH,
    LOAD,
    STORE,
    ADD,
    SUB,
    MUL,
    DIV,
    MOD,
    NEG,
    EQ,
    NE,
    LT,
    LE,
    GT,
    GE,
    AND,
    OR,
    NOT,
    HALT,
)


class CompileError(Exception):
    """Raised when the compiler encounters an unsupported construct or a
    semantic problem such as an undefined variable.
    """

    pass


class Compiler:
    """
    Core compiler class.

    Usage
    -----
    >>> compiler = Compiler()
    >>> instructions = compiler.compile(program)
    """

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        # List[Tuple[Mnemonic, Any]] – the final instruction stream
        self.instructions: List[Tuple[Any, Any]] = []

        # Variable → slot index mapping (canonical state contract)
        self.slots: dict[str, int] = {}

        # Next free slot number
        self._next_slot: int = 0

    # --------------------------------------------------------------------- #
    # Public API
    # --------------------------------------------------------------------- #
    def compile(self, program: Program) -> List[Tuple[Any, Any]]:
        """
        Compile a ``Program`` AST into a list of assembly instructions.

        The returned list follows the canonical *Instruction list* contract:
        ``list[tuple(Mnemonic, operand?)]`` where ``operand`` is ``None`` for
        stack‑only operations.

        A ``HALT`` instruction is always appended as the final operation.
        """
        # Reset internal state for each compilation request
        self.instructions = []
        self.slots = {}
        self._next_slot = 0

        # -----------------------------------------------------------------
        # 1. Compile top‑level statements (e.g., let‑bindings)
        # -----------------------------------------------------------------
        stmt_collection = None
        if hasattr(program, "stmts"):
            stmt_collection = program.stmts
        elif hasattr(program, "statements"):
            stmt_collection = program.statements

        if stmt_collection is not None:
            for stmt in stmt_collection:
                self._compile_stmt(stmt)

        # -----------------------------------------------------------------
        # 2. Compile the final expression (or the program itself if it is an
        #    expression)
        # -----------------------------------------------------------------
        if hasattr(program, "expr"):
            self._compile_expr(program.expr)
        else:
            # Fallback: treat the whole ``program`` as an expression node.
            self._compile_expr(program)

        # -----------------------------------------------------------------
        # 3. Terminate with HALT
        # -----------------------------------------------------------------
        self.instructions.append((HALT, None))
        return self.instructions

    # --------------------------------------------------------------------- #
    # Statement handling
    # --------------------------------------------------------------------- #
    def _compile_stmt(self, stmt: Any) -> None:
        """
        Currently the only supported statement type is ``LetStmt``.
        """
        if isinstance(stmt, LetStmt):
            # Extract variable name – ``LetStmt`` may expose it as ``name`` or
            # ``var`` (the latter being a ``Variable`` node).
            var_name = getattr(stmt, "name", None)
            if var_name is None:
                var_node = getattr(stmt, "var", None)
                if isinstance(var_node, Variable):
                    var_name = var_node.name
                else:
                    raise CompileError(f"LetStmt missing variable identifier: {stmt!r}")

            # Compile the bound expression.
            expr_node = getattr(stmt, "expr", None)
            if expr_node is None:
                # Fallback for older AST versions that used ``value``.
                expr_node = getattr(stmt, "value", None)

            if expr_node is None:
                raise CompileError(f"LetStmt missing bound expression: {stmt!r}")

            self._compile_expr(expr_node)

            # Allocate a slot for the variable (if not already allocated).
            slot = self.slots.get(var_name)
            if slot is None:
                slot = self._next_slot
                self.slots[var_name] = slot
                self._next_slot += 1

            # Store the computed value into the slot.
            self.instructions.append((STORE, slot))
        else:
            raise CompileError(f"Unsupported statement type: {type(stmt)}")

    # --------------------------------------------------------------------- #
    # Expression handling (post‑order traversal)
    # --------------------------------------------------------------------- #
    def _compile_expr(self, expr: Any) -> None:
        """
        Recursively compile an expression node into instructions.
        The compilation order is post‑order: sub‑expressions first,
        then the operator that combines them.
        """

        # Literals
        # -----------------------------------------------------------------
        if isinstance(expr, Literal):
            # ``Literal`` is expected to expose its concrete value via ``value``.
            value = getattr(expr, "value", None)
            self.instructions.append((PUSH, value))
            return

        # Variable reference
        # -----------------------------------------------------------------
        if isinstance(expr, Variable):
            var_name = getattr(expr, "name", None)
            if var_name is None:
                raise CompileError(f"Variable node missing name: {expr!r}")

            slot = self.slots.get(var_name)
            if slot is None:
                raise CompileError(f"Undefined variable referenced: {var_name}")

"""AST node definitions for the ExprC language.

The compiler, assembler and VM work with these concrete syntax‑tree
objects.  All nodes are immutable dataclasses; they expose their
children via a ``children`` property to simplify visitor implementations.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import List, Tuple, Union

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Base type for all AST nodes – useful for type‑checking and visitors.
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
ASTNode = Union[
    "Literal",
    "Variable",
    "UnaryOp",
    "BinaryOp",
    "LetStmt",
    "Program",
]

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Literal values
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
Scalar = Union[int, float, bool]


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class Literal:
    """A scalar literal (int, float or bool)."""

    value: Scalar

    def __repr__(self) -> str:
        return f"Literal({self.value!r})"

    @property
    def children(self) -> Tuple[()]:
        """Literals have no child nodes."""
        return ()


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Variable reference
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class Variable:
    """Reference to a variable by name."""

    name: str

    def __repr__(self) -> str:
        return f"Variable({self.name!r})"

    @property
    def children(self) -> Tuple[()]:
        """Variables have no child nodes."""
        return ()


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Unary operation
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class UnaryOp:
    """Unary operator applied to a single operand.

    ``op`` is the textual representation used by the parser
    (e.g. '-', '!', '+').
    """

    op: str
    operand: ASTNode

    def __repr__(self) -> str:
        return f"UnaryOp({self.op!r}, {self.operand!r})"

    @property
    def children(self) -> Tuple[ASTNode]:
        return (self.operand,)


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Binary operation
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class BinaryOp:
    """Binary operator with left and right operands.

    ``op`` is the textual representation used by the parser
    (e.g. '+', '-', '*', '/', '==', '&&', ...).
    """

    left: ASTNode
    op: str
    right: ASTNode

    def __repr__(self) -> str:
        return f"BinaryOp({self.left!r}, {self.op!r}, {self.right!r})"

    @property
    def children(self) -> Tuple[ASTNode, ASTNode]:
        return (self.left, self.right)


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Let statement – introduces a new variable binding.
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class LetStmt:
    """`let <name> = <expr>` statement."""

    name: str
    expr: ASTNode

    def __repr__(self) -> str:
        return f"LetStmt({self.name!r}, {self.expr!r})"

    @property
    def children(self) -> Tuple[ASTNode]:
        return (self.expr,)


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Program root node – a sequence of statements.
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class Program:
    """Root of the AST; holds an ordered list of statements."""

    stmts: List[ASTNode]

    def __repr__(self) -> str:
        return f"Program({self.stmts!r})"

    def children(self) -> Tuple[ASTNode, ...]:

"""
Compiler for the exprc language.

Transforms an abstract syntax tree (AST) into a linear list of assembly
mnemonics suitable for the assembler / virtual machine.

The compilation strategy is **post‑order emission**:
sub‑expressions are compiled first, then the operator that combines them.
Let‑bindings allocate slots in a variable table and use STORE/LOAD to
persist values across the program.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Any, List, Tuple

# AST node classes and program container
# NOTE: These symbols live in ``exprc.ast``; importing directly from the
# package root caused an ImportError because ``exprc.__init__`` does not
# re‑export them.
from exprc.ast import (
    Program,
    LetStmt,
    Variable,
    Literal,
    UnaryOp,
    BinaryOp,
)

# Mnemonic constants – each is emitted as a tuple (Mnemonic, operand?)
# NOTE: Mnemonics are defined in ``exprc.instructions``. Importing from the
# package root fails for the same reason as above.
from exprc.instructions import (
    PUSH,
    LOAD,
    STORE,
    ADD,
    SUB,
    MUL,
    DIV,
    MOD,
    NEG,
    EQ,
    NE,
    LT,
    LE,
    GT,
    GE,
    AND,
    OR,
    NOT,
    HALT,
)


class CompileError(Exception):
    """Raised when the compiler encounters an unsupported construct or a
    semantic problem such as an undefined variable.
    """

    pass


class Compiler:
    """
    Core compiler class.

    Usage
    -----
    >>> compiler = Compiler()
    >>> instructions = compiler.compile(program)
    """

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        # List[Tuple[Mnemonic, Any]] – the final instruction stream
        self.instructions: List[Tuple[Any, Any]] = []

        # Variable → slot index mapping (canonical state contract)
        self.slots: dict[str, int] = {}

        # Next free slot number
        self._next_slot: int = 0

    # --------------------------------------------------------------------- #
    # Public API
    # --------------------------------------------------------------------- #
    def compile(self, program: Program) -> List[Tuple[Any, Any]]:
        """
        Compile a ``Program`` AST into a list of assembly instructions.

        The returned list follows the canonical *Instruction list* contract:
        ``list[tuple(Mnemonic, operand?)]`` where ``operand`` is ``None`` for
        stack‑only operations.

        A ``HALT`` instruction is always appended as the final operation.
        """
        # Reset internal state for each compilation request
        self.instructions = []
        self.slots = {}
        self._next_slot = 0

        # -----------------------------------------------------------------
        # 1. Compile top‑level statements (e.g., let‑bindings)
        # -----------------------------------------------------------------
        stmt_collection = None
        if hasattr(program, "stmts"):
            stmt_collection = program.stmts
        elif hasattr(program, "statements"):
            stmt_collection = program.statements

        if stmt_collection is not None:
            for stmt in stmt_collection:
                self._compile_stmt(stmt)

        # -----------------------------------------------------------------
        # 2. Compile the final expression (or the program itself if it is an
        #    expression)
        # -----------------------------------------------------------------
        if hasattr(program, "expr"):
            self._compile_expr(program.expr)
        else:
            # Fallback: treat the whole ``program`` as an expression node.
            self._compile_expr(program)

        # -----------------------------------------------------------------
        # 3. Terminate with HALT
        # -----------------------------------------------------------------
        self.instructions.append((HALT, None))
        return self.instructions

    # --------------------------------------------------------------------- #
    # Statement handling
    # --------------------------------------------------------------------- #
    def _compile_stmt(self, stmt: Any) -> None:
        """
        Compile a top‑level statement.

        Supported statements:
        * LetStmt – variable declaration/assignment.
        * Expression nodes (Literal, Variable, UnaryOp, BinaryOp) – evaluate the
          expression and discard the result (as in a REPL expression statement).

        Any other node type raises ``CompileError``.
        """
        # ------------------------------------------------------------------
        # Handle variable declarations.
        # ------------------------------------------------------------------
        if isinstance(stmt, LetStmt):
            # Extract the variable name.  Different AST versions expose it as
            # ``name`` (a string) or ``var`` (a ``Variable`` node).
            var_name = getattr(stmt, "name", None)
            if var_name is None:
                var_node = getattr(stmt, "var", None)
                if isinstance(var_node, Variable):
                    var_name = var_node.name
                else:
                    raise CompileError(f"LetStmt missing variable identifier: {stmt!r}")

            # Extract the bound expression.  Older ASTs may use ``value``.
            expr_node = getattr(stmt, "expr", None)
            if expr_node is None:
                expr_node = getattr(stmt, "value", None)

            if expr_node is None:
                raise CompileError(f"LetStmt missing bound expression: {stmt!r}")

            # Compile the RHS expression.
            self._compile_expr(expr_node)

            # Allocate a slot for the variable if it does not already exist.
            slot = self.slots.get(var_name)
            if slot is None:
                slot = self._next_slot
                self.slots[var_name] = slot
                self._next_slot += 1

            # Store the computed value into the allocated slot.
            self.instructions.append((STORE, slot))
            return

        # ------------------------------------------------------------------
        # Handle top‑level expression statements.
        # ------------------------------------------------------------------
        # The parser may produce bare expression nodes as statements (e.g.
        # a literal or variable reference).  We compile the expression to
        # evaluate it, then discard the result by popping the stack.  This
        # mirrors typical REPL behaviour where the value is printed but not
        # retained.
        if isinstance(stmt, (Literal, Variable, UnaryOp, BinaryOp)):
            self._compile_expr(stmt)
            # Discard the expression result; the VM will have pushed it onto
            # the operand stack.  POP removes it without affecting program state.
            self.instructions.append((POP, None))
            return

        # ------------------------------------------------------------------
        # Anything else is unsupported.
        # ------------------------------------------------------------------
        raise CompileError(f"Unsupported statement type: {type(stmt)}")

The VM executes a list of instructions produced by the compiler/assembler.

        Parameters

            The program to execute.  Each tuple consists of a mnemonic and an
            optional operand (``None`` for stack‑only operations).

        Returns
        -------

            unknown mnemonic).

        for mnemonic, operand in instructions:

    def _dispatch(self, mnemonic: Mnemonic, operand: Any) -> None:
        """Map a mnemonic to its implementation method."""
        dispatch_map: Dict[Mnemonic, Callable[[Any], None]] = {

            Mnemonic.LOAD: self._op_load,
            Mnemonic.STORE: self._op_store,
            Mnemonic.ADD: self._op_add,
            Mnemonic.SUB: self._op_sub,
            Mnemonic.MUL: self._op_mul,
            Mnemonic.DIV: self._op_div,
            Mnemonic.MOD: self._op_mod,
            Mnemonic.NEG: self._op_neg,
            Mnemonic.NOT: self._op_not,
            Mnemonic.AND: self._op_and,
            Mnemonic.OR: self._op_or,
            Mnemonic.EQ: self._op_eq,
            Mnemonic.NEQ: self._op_neq,
            Mnemonic.LT: self._op_lt,
            Mnemonic.GT: self._op_gt,
            Mnemonic.LE: self._op_le,
            Mnemonic.GE: self._op_ge,

        if value is None:
            raise RuntimeError(f"Variable '{operand}' accessed before initialization")

        slot = self._var_slots[operand]

        right = self._pop()
        left = self._pop()
        self._push(func(left, right))

    def _op_add(self, _: Any) -> None:
        self._binary_op(lambda a, b: a + b)

    def _op_sub(self, _: Any) -> None:
        self._binary_op(lambda a, b: a - b)

    def _op_mul(self, _: Any) -> None:
        self._binary_op(lambda a, b: a * b)

    def _op_div(self, _: Any) -> None:
        right = self._pop()
        left = self._pop()
        if right == 0:
            raise RuntimeError("Division by zero")
        self._push(left / right)

    def _op_mod(self, _: Any) -> None:
        right = self._pop()
        left = self._pop()
        if right == 0:

        self._push(left % right)

"""
Instruction set definition for the ExprC stack‑machine.

This module declares the ISA mnemonics as an ``IntEnum`` and provides a
light‑weight helper to create instruction tuples that conform to the
canonical *Instruction list* contract:

    List[Tuple[Mnemonic, Optional[Any]]]

Each instruction is represented as a two‑element tuple where the second
element is ``None`` for stack‑only operations or holds a literal/value
for instructions such as ``PUSH``, ``LOAD`` and ``STORE``.

The exported symbols are:
    - Mnemonic   – the enumeration of opcodes.
    - PUSH, LOAD, STORE, ADD, SUB, MUL, DIV, MOD,
      NEG, EQ, NE, LT, LE, GT, GE, AND, OR, NOT, HALT,
      POP, DUP, SWAP – convenience aliases for the enum members.
    - encode     – helper that builds a correctly‑typed instruction tuple.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from enum import IntEnum, auto
from typing import Any, Tuple, Optional

# Public interface – includes stack‑manipulation mnemonics required by the VM.
__all__ = [
    "Mnemonic",
    "PUSH",
    "LOAD",
    "STORE",
    "ADD",
    "SUB",
    "MUL",
    "DIV",
    "MOD",

    "HALT",
    # Stack manipulation mnemonics added for full VM support
    "POP",
    "DUP",
    "SWAP",
    "encode",
]


class Mnemonic(IntEnum):
    """Enumeration of all stack‑machine opcodes.

    The integer values are generated automatically; they are stable
    within a single interpreter session and are used by the assembler
    when translating source code to bytecode.
    """

    # Stack manipulation / literals
    PUSH = auto()  # operand: literal scalar (int, float, bool)
    LOAD = auto()  # operand: variable name (str) – push variable value
    STORE = auto()  # operand: variable name (str) – pop and store

    # Arithmetic
    ADD = auto()  # pop two, push a + b
    SUB = auto()  # pop two, push a - b
    MUL = auto()  # pop two, push a * b
    DIV = auto()  # pop two, push a / b (integer division for ints)
    MOD = auto()  # pop two, push a % b
    NEG = auto()  # pop one, push -a

    # Comparison
    EQ = auto()  # pop two, push a == b
    NE = auto()  # pop two, push a != b
    LT = auto()  # pop two, push a < b
    LE = auto()  # pop two, push a <= b
    GT = auto()  # pop two, push a > b
    GE = auto()  # pop two, push a >= b

    # Logical
    AND = auto()  # pop two, push a and b (bool)
    OR = auto()  # pop two, push a or b (bool)
    NOT = auto()  # pop one, push not a (bool)

    # Control
    HALT = auto()  # stop execution

    # Stack manipulation – required by the compiler and VM.
    POP = auto()   # operand: None – discard top of stack
    DUP = auto()   # operand: None – duplicate top of stack
    SWAP = auto()  # operand: None – swap top two stack values

# Convenience aliases – they make the rest of the codebase read like
# assembly language without having to reference the enum class each time.
PUSH = Mnemonic.PUSH
LOAD = Mnemonic.LOAD
STORE = Mnemonic.STORE
ADD = Mnemonic.ADD
SUB = Mnemonic.SUB
MUL = Mnemonic.MUL
DIV = Mnemonic.DIV
MOD = Mnemonic.MOD
NEG = Mnemonic.NEG
EQ = Mnemonic.EQ
NE = Mnemonic.NE
LT = Mnemonic.LT
LE = Mnemonic.LE
GT = Mnemonic.GT
GE = Mnemonic.GE
AND = Mnemonic.AND
OR = Mnemonic.OR
NOT = Mnemonic.NOT
HALT = Mnemonic.HALT
POP = Mnemonic.POP
DUP = Mnemonic.DUP
SWAP = Mnemonic.SWAP


def encode(mnemonic: Mnemonic, operand: Optional[Any] = None) -> Tuple[Mnemonic, Optional[Any]]:
    """Build a canonical instruction tuple.

    Parameters
    ----------
    mnemonic:
        The opcode to emit. Must be a member of :class:`Mnemonic`.
    operand:
        The optional operand associated with the opcode.
        For stack‑only operations (e.g., ``ADD``) this should be ``None``.
        For ``PUSH``, ``LOAD`` and ``STORE`` it holds the literal value
        or variable name respectively.

    Returns
    -------
    Tuple[Mnemonic, Optional[Any]]
        A two‑element tuple that conforms to the *Instruction list* contract
        used throughout the compiler, assembler and VM.
    """
    if not isinstance(mnemonic, Mnemonic):
        raise TypeError(
            f"mnemonic must be an instance of Mnemonic enum, got {type(mnemonic)!r}"
        )

    # No further validation of operand is performed here; the VM will
    # raise appropriate errors if an unexpected type/value is encountered.
    return (mnemonic, operand)

"""
Compiler for the exprc language.

Transforms an abstract syntax tree (AST) into a linear list of assembly
mnemonics suitable for the assembler / virtual machine.

The compilation strategy is **post‑order emission**:
sub‑expressions are compiled first, then the operator that combines them.
Let‑bindings allocate slots in a variable table and use STORE/LOAD to
persist values across the program.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Any, List, Tuple

# AST node classes and program container
# NOTE: These symbols live in ``exprc.ast``; importing directly from the
# package root caused an ImportError because ``exprc.__init__`` does not

)

    OR,
    NOT,
    HALT,
)


class CompileError(Exception):
    """Raised when the compiler encounters an unsupported construct or a
    semantic problem such as an undefined variable.
    """

    pass


class Compiler:
    """
    Core compiler class.

    Usage
    -----
    >>> compiler = Compiler()
    >>> instructions = compiler.compile(program)
    """

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        # List[Tuple[Mnemonic, Any]] – the final instruction stream
        self.instructions: List[Tuple[Any, Any]] = []

        # Variable → slot index mapping (canonical state contract)
        self.slots: dict[str, int] = {}

        # Next free slot number
        self._next_slot: int = 0

    # --------------------------------------------------------------------- #
    # Public API
    # --------------------------------------------------------------------- #
    def compile(self, program: Program) -> List[Tuple[Any, Any]]:
        """
        Compile a ``Program`` AST into a list of assembly instructions.

        The returned list follows the canonical *Instruction list* contract:
        ``list[tuple(Mnemonic, operand?)]`` where ``operand`` is ``None`` for
        stack‑only operations.

        A ``HALT`` instruction is always appended as the final operation.
        """
        # Reset internal state for each compilation request
        self.instructions = []
        self.slots = {}
        self._next_slot = 0

        # -----------------------------------------------------------------
        # 1. Compile top‑level statements (e.g., let‑bindings)
        # -----------------------------------------------------------------
        stmt_collection = None
        if hasattr(program, "stmts"):
            stmt_collection = program.stmts
        elif hasattr(program, "statements"):
            stmt_collection = program.statements

        if stmt_collection is not None:
            for stmt in stmt_collection:
                self._compile_stmt(stmt)

        # -----------------------------------------------------------------
        # 2. Compile the final expression (or the program itself if it is an
        #    expression)
        # -----------------------------------------------------------------
        if hasattr(program, "expr"):
            self._compile_expr(program.expr)

"""
Instruction set definition for the ExprC stack‑machine.

This module declares the ISA mnemonics as an ``IntEnum`` and provides a
light‑weight helper to create instruction tuples that conform to the
canonical *Instruction list* contract:

    List[Tuple[Mnemonic, Optional[Any]]]

Each instruction is represented as a two‑element tuple where the second
element is ``None`` for stack‑only operations or holds a literal/value
for instructions such as ``PUSH``, ``LOAD`` and ``STORE``.

The exported symbols are:
    - Mnemonic   – the enumeration of opcodes.
    - PUSH, LOAD, STORE, ADD, SUB, MUL, DIV, MOD,
      NEG, EQ, NE, LT, LE, GT, GE, AND, OR, NOT, HALT,
      POP, DUP, SWAP – convenience aliases for the enum members.
    - encode     – helper that builds a correctly‑typed instruction tuple.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from enum import IntEnum, auto
from typing import Any, Tuple, Optional

# Public interface – includes stack‑manipulation mnemonics required by the VM.
__all__ = [
    "Mnemonic",
    "PUSH",
    "LOAD",
    "STORE",
    "ADD",
    "SUB",
    "MUL",
    "DIV",
    "MOD",
    "NEG",
    "EQ",
    "NE",
    "LT",
    "LE",
    "GT",
    "GE",
    "AND",
    "OR",
    "NOT",
    "HALT",
    # Stack manipulation mnemonics added for full VM support
    "POP",
    "DUP",
    "SWAP",
    "encode",
]


class Mnemonic(IntEnum):
    """Enumeration of all stack‑machine opcodes.

    The integer values are generated automatically; they are stable
    within a single interpreter session and are used by the assembler
    when translating source code to bytecode.
    """

    # Stack manipulation / literals
    PUSH = auto()  # operand: literal scalar (int, float, bool)
    LOAD = auto()  # operand: variable name (str) – push variable value
    STORE = auto()  # operand: variable name (str) – pop and store

    # Arithmetic
    ADD = auto()  # pop two, push a + b
    SUB = auto()  # pop two, push a - b
    MUL = auto()  # pop two, push a * b
    DIV = auto()  # pop two, push a / b (integer division for ints)
    MOD = auto()  # pop two, push a % b
    NEG = auto()  # pop one, push -a

    # Comparison
    EQ = auto()  # pop two, push a == b
    NE = auto()  # pop two, push a != b
    LT = auto()  # pop two, push a < b
    LE = auto()  # pop two, push a <= b
    GT = auto()  # pop two, push a > b
    GE = auto()  # pop two, push a >= b

    # Logical
    AND = auto()  # pop two, push a and b (bool)
    OR = auto()  # pop two, push a or b (bool)
    NOT = auto()  # pop one, push not a (bool)

    # Control
    HALT = auto()  # stop execution

    # Stack manipulation – required by the compiler and VM.
    POP = auto()   # operand: None – discard top of stack
    DUP = auto()   # operand: None – duplicate top of stack
    SWAP = auto()  # operand: None – swap top two stack values

# Convenience aliases – they make the rest of the codebase read like
# assembly language without having to reference the enum class each time.
PUSH = Mnemonic.PUSH
LOAD = Mnemonic.LOAD
STORE = Mnemonic.STORE
ADD = Mnemonic.ADD
SUB = Mnemonic.SUB
MUL = Mnemonic.MUL
DIV = Mnemonic.DIV
MOD = Mnemonic.MOD
NEG = Mnemonic.NEG
EQ = Mnemonic.EQ
NE = Mnemonic.NE
LT = Mnemonic.LT
LE = Mnemonic.LE
GT = Mnemonic.GT
GE = Mnemonic.GE
AND = Mnemonic.AND
OR = Mnemonic.OR
NOT = Mnemonic.NOT
HALT = Mnemonic.HALT
POP = Mnemonic.POP
DUP = Mnemonic.DUP
SWAP = Mnemonic.SWAP


def encode(mnemonic: Mnemonic, operand: Optional[Any] = None) -> Tuple[Mnemonic, Optional[Any]]:
    """Build a canonical instruction tuple.

    Parameters
    ----------
    mnemonic:
        The opcode to emit. Must be a member of :class:`Mnemonic`.
    operand:
        The optional operand associated with the opcode.
        For stack‑only operations (e.g., ``ADD``) this should be ``None``.
        For ``PUSH``, ``LOAD`` and ``STORE`` it holds the literal value
        or variable name respectively.

    Returns
    -------
    Tuple[Mnemonic, Optional[Any]]
        A two‑element tuple that conforms to the *Instruction list* contract
        used throughout the compiler, assembler and VM.
    """
    if not isinstance(mnemonic, Mnemonic):
        raise TypeError(
            f"mnemonic must be an instance of Mnemonic enum, got {type(mnemonic)!r}"
        )

    # No further validation of operand is performed here; the VM will
    # raise appropriate errors if an unexpected type/value is encountered.
    return (mnemonic, operand)

objects.  All nodes are immutable dataclasses; they expose their
children via a ``children`` property to simplify visitor implementations.

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import List, Tuple, Union

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Base type for all AST nodes – useful for type‑checking and visitors.
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
ASTNode = Union[
    "Literal",
    "Variable",
    "UnaryOp",
    "BinaryOp",
    "LetStmt",
    "Program",
]

# Literal values
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
Scalar = Union[int, float, bool]


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class Literal:
    """A scalar literal (int, float or bool)."""

    value: Scalar

    def __repr__(self) -> str:
        return f"Literal({self.value!r})"

    @property
    def children(self) -> Tuple[()]:
        """Literals have no child nodes."""
        return ()


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Variable reference
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class Variable:
    """Reference to a variable by name."""

    name: str

    def __repr__(self) -> str:
        return f"Variable({self.name!r})"

    @property
    def children(self) -> Tuple[()]:
        """Variables have no child nodes."""
        return ()


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Unary operation
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class UnaryOp:
    """Unary operator applied to a single operand.

    ``op`` is the textual representation used by the parser
    (e.g. '-', '!', '+').
    """

    op: str
    operand: ASTNode

    def __repr__(self) -> str:
        return f"UnaryOp({self.op!r}, {self.operand!r})"

    @property
    def children(self) -> Tuple[ASTNode]:
        return (self.operand,)


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Binary operation
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class BinaryOp:
    """Binary operator with left and right operands.

    ``op`` is the textual representation used by the parser
    (e.g. '+', '-', '*', '/', '==', '&&', ...).
    """

    left: ASTNode
    op: str
    right: ASTNode

    def __repr__(self) -> str:
        return f"BinaryOp({self.left!r}, {self.op!r}, {self.right!r})"

    @property
    def children(self) -> Tuple[ASTNode, ASTNode]:
        return (self.left, self.right)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------

        return f"LetStmt({self.name!r}, {self.expr!r})"

    def children(self) -> Tuple[ASTNode]:

This module declares the ISA mnemonics as an ``IntEnum`` and provides a
light‑weight helper to create instruction tuples that conform to the
canonical *Instruction list* contract:

    """Enumeration of all stack‑machine opcodes.

    The integer values are generated automatically; they are stable
    within a single interpreter session and are used by the assembler
    when translating source code to bytecode.

    # Stack manipulation / literals
    PUSH = auto()  # operand: literal scalar (int, float, bool)
    LOAD = auto()  # operand: variable name (str) – push variable value
    STORE = auto()  # operand: variable name (str) – pop and store

    # Arithmetic
    ADD = auto()  # pop two, push a + b
    SUB = auto()  # pop two, push a - b
    MUL = auto()  # pop two, push a * b
    DIV = auto()  # pop two, push a / b (integer division for ints)
    MOD = auto()  # pop two, push a % b
    NEG = auto()  # pop one, push -a

    # Comparison
    EQ = auto()  # pop two, push a == b
    NE = auto()  # pop two, push a != b
    LT = auto()  # pop two, push a < b
    LE = auto()  # pop two, push a <= b
    GT = auto()  # pop two, push a > b
    GE = auto()  # pop two, push a >= b

    # Logical
    AND = auto()  # pop two, push a and b (bool)
    OR = auto()  # pop two, push a or b (bool)
    NOT = auto()  # pop one, push not a (bool)

    # Control
    HALT = auto()  # stop execution

    # Stack manipulation – required by the compiler and VM.
    POP = auto()   # operand: None – discard top of stack
    DUP = auto()   # operand: None – duplicate top of stack
    SWAP = auto()  # operand: None – swap top two stack values

LOAD = Mnemonic.LOAD
STORE = Mnemonic.STORE
ADD = Mnemonic.ADD
SUB = Mnemonic.SUB
MUL = Mnemonic.MUL
DIV = Mnemonic.DIV

OR = Mnemonic.OR
NOT = Mnemonic.NOT
HALT = Mnemonic.HALT
POP = Mnemonic.POP
DUP = Mnemonic.DUP
SWAP = Mnemonic.SWAP


def encode(mnemonic: Mnemonic, operand: Optional[Any] = None) -> Tuple[Mnemonic, Optional[Any]]:
    """Build a canonical instruction tuple.

    Parameters
    ----------
    mnemonic:
        The opcode to emit. Must be a member of :class:`Mnemonic`.
    operand:
        The optional operand associated with the opcode.
        For stack‑only operations (e.g., ``ADD``) this should be ``None``.
        For ``PUSH``, ``LOAD`` and ``STORE`` it holds the literal value
        or variable name respectively.

    Returns
    -------
    Tuple[Mnemonic, Optional[Any]]
        A two‑element tuple that conforms to the *Instruction list* contract
        used throughout the compiler, assembler and VM.
    """
    if not isinstance(mnemonic, Mnemonic):
        raise TypeError(
            f"mnemonic must be an instance of Mnemonic enum, got {type(mnemonic)!r}"
        )

    # No further validation of operand is performed here; the VM will
    # raise appropriate errors if an unexpected type/value is encountered.
    return (mnemonic, operand)

"""
Instruction set definition for the ExprC stack‑machine.

This module declares the ISA mnemonics as an ``IntEnum`` and provides a
light‑weight helper to create instruction tuples that conform to the
canonical *Instruction list* contract:

    List[Tuple[Mnemonic, Optional[Any]]]

Each instruction is represented as a two‑element tuple where the second
element is ``None`` for stack‑only operations or holds a literal/value
for instructions such as ``PUSH``, ``LOAD`` and ``STORE``.

The exported symbols are:
    - Mnemonic   – the enumeration of opcodes.
    - PUSH, LOAD, STORE, ADD, SUB, MUL, DIV, MOD,
      NEG, EQ, NE, LT, LE, GT, GE, AND, OR, NOT, HALT,
      POP, DUP, SWAP – convenience aliases for the enum members.
    - encode     – helper that builds a correctly‑typed instruction tuple.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from enum import IntEnum, auto
from typing import Any, Tuple, Optional

# Public interface – includes stack‑manipulation mnemonics required by the VM.
__all__ = [
    "Mnemonic",
    "PUSH",
    "LOAD",
    "STORE",
    "ADD",
    "SUB",
    "MUL",
    "DIV",
    "MOD",
    "NEG",
    "EQ",
    "NE",
    "LT",
    "LE",
    "GT",

    "AND",
    "OR",
    "NOT",
    "HALT",
    # Stack manipulation mnemonics added for full VM support
    "POP",
    "DUP",
    "SWAP",
    "encode",
]


class Mnemonic(IntEnum):
    """Enumeration of all stack‑machine opcodes.

    The integer values are generated automatically; they are stable
    within a single interpreter session and are used by the assembler
    when translating source code to bytecode.
    """

    # Stack manipulation / literals
    PUSH = auto()  # operand: literal scalar (int, float, bool)
    LOAD = auto()  # operand: variable name (str) – push variable value
    STORE = auto()  # operand: variable name (str) – pop and store

    # Arithmetic
    ADD = auto()  # pop two, push a + b
    SUB = auto()  # pop two, push a - b
    MUL = auto()  # pop two, push a * b
    DIV = auto()  # pop two, push a / b (integer division for ints)
    MOD = auto()  # pop two, push a % b
    NEG = auto()  # pop one, push -a

    # Comparison
    EQ = auto()  # pop two, push a == b
    NE = auto()  # pop two, push a != b
    LT = auto()  # pop two, push a < b
    LE = auto()  # pop two, push a <= b
    GT = auto()  # pop two, push a > b
    GE = auto()  # pop two, push a >= b

    # Logical
    AND = auto()  # pop two, push a and b (bool)
    OR = auto()  # pop two, push a or b (bool)
    NOT = auto()  # pop one, push not a (bool)

    # Control
    HALT = auto()  # stop execution

    # Stack manipulation – required by the compiler and VM.
    POP = auto()   # operand: None – discard top of stack
    DUP = auto()   # operand: None – duplicate top of stack
    SWAP = auto()  # operand: None – swap top two stack values
